I would try to get out of this class.
Assignment directions are very unclelar. His class is very confusing.I dont reccomend.

analysis.name: Jeff Ackerman
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 89 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He does not allow his students to use calculators on his exams. If you know anything about economics, especially Macroeconomics, there are many calculations involved, and it seems unfair that you can't use a calculator on the exams when they have complex formulas. Other professors allow a caclulator so I suggest you take one of their courses.

I loved learning about economics in high school. Unfortunately, this professor has now ruined the subject for me. He somehow found a way to make it a mundane, boring chore. It is extremely lecture-heavy, and I felt he explained things in an unnecessarily complicated manner. Ackerman is extremely inaccessible as well.

Professor Ackermann successfully (jokingly) catfished me into becoming an economics major. He actually made economics interesting and fun to learn, which in turn made me think the department was all like that. Boy was I wrong, almost every other Econ professor outside of him is monotone, boring, and old. I enjoyed Econ when I had him, now I don't.

Literally the funniest prof ever. Such an amazing guy and you can really tell that he cares abt the class and has passion for what he does. I was undecided before coming to college but after taking his class, made me want to pursue an econ degree. Funny lectures, 3 midterms and 1 final exam but only 3 exam grades count, really helpful study guides.

I would say that this class is pretty doable as a freshman. He gives a lot of resources and I believe that the homework assignments (both completion and accuracy) and especially the study guides both give a lot of information to help when it comes to exams. This class demands a lot of effort though so make sure you're staying on track.

analysis.name: Amanda Lorenz-Reaves
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: I could say the class is easy, or I could say that the material was explained so well and so well understood that the class seemed easy. Isn't that the goal as a good teacher to ensure students are learning all the material? Mission accomplished.

Clearly passionate about her lectures and it shows, they were all super easy to follow and interesting. The 2 Homework assignments are fun and don't take much time. In class participation assignments create interesting discussions, and students go to the MSU bug house at the end of the semester!

LOVEDDD Dr. Lorenz! She is very sweet and funny. This is an online class held over zoom so you'll have daily in class participation and pre-class readings, 3 home work, and 4 exams (all of which are open note). Genuinely enjoyed this class as her lectures are interesting and you can tell she is passionate about her work. Could not recommend enough!

I adored Professor Lorenz! She was incredibly gracious with RCPD extensions, and provided stress-free assignments. Every quiz and test was open resource, with plenty of time to complete the task. Lectures were engaging and interesting. She felicitated a calming learning environment while also sharing her passions. I cannot recommend enough!

Easiest ISB 201 class if you are willing to show up to class. She does in class papers for attendance (so easy you barely have to pay attention) basically your entire grade is attendance, a few 1 page papers & exams. The exams are very very easy. Super kind prof! Highly recommend her but dont get stuck in the 8:30am you wont make it.

analysis.name: Alena Aniskiewicz

Dr. A is one of the most respectful and reasonable professors I've had. She makes the material very interesting and fun to learn about. I will say that she does ask the class questions about the films and asks you to discuss with peers, but overall this class was great!

Great Professor!! Loved the class, and it was fairly easy. There is a lot of group discussion and one group project. Attendance was mandatory but you're allowed 2 skips. 5 pop quizzes throughout the semester on the course material. I would recommend this professor.

Alena was very nice and you could tell she cares about this class! I enjoyed the content but the class but too long imo. Lots of participation, group work, and talking with the person next to you so get ready for that. I often felt bad because not a lot of people would participate during class. But super easy class and assignments, highly recommend

analysis.name: Alexandra Allweiss

Alex was an amazing instructor who clearly cared about her students and the material she taught. She kept the class engaged and knew how to pull us back in when attention drifted. Alex was a great professor, and I really enjoyed her class. She was so caring and respectful of everyone in class and what they thought. I took Alex's TE 353 class, and she was awesome! Super interesting lectures and in-depth discussions. She clearly is very knowledgable and passionate about our material and is so caring for us and our needs. Classes were dynamic and so fun to attend every time, plus she brought food every week. I loved this class and would love to have Alex again!!
Alex cares very much what her students think. She works hard to make sure everyone understands the homework, but she also expects you to bring your perspective into the discussion.

Please for the love of God and your sanity do not take this class. It's only week 4 and it makes me want to die. Its unorganized, poorly structured, too much going on, and classes are overwhelming and vague. Please just don't take this class.

analysis.name: Albert Azadnia
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Azadnia doesn't come around much; TA-based. TA is either super critical or lenient. In my experience, TA explained the procedures so vaguely and we were confused most of the time. Really unfair that we're graded on purity/yield when the syllubus procedures are inaccurate and outdated. Difficult to prepare for labs. Goodluck!!

TA-based. Lab reports are short, and labs are mainly repeats of CEM 355. Literature assignments are annoying but easy when you know what you're doing. The last two labs (finding unknown compounds) take the most amount of time, so make sure you get comfortable with taking IR, NMR, and the melting point!

TA-based, but if you have Jenna Lepek, you'll do great! Gives you the procedures before class and helps you perform them. Some labs are based on attendance, while others on yield and appearance. Overall, a simple class if you come and do the procedure. Dr. Azadnia himself doesn't teach, but he grades your final paper at the end—pretty fair graders

Doctor Azadnia runs the overall course so you will likely never run into him; however from my interactions he is very kind and easy-going. This course is entirely based on your TA for most of the grading involving labs and etc. Lab procedures can often be confusing and you basically have to attend every lab to get a 4.0.

TA based. Lab reports are mostly based on effort, but some labs (and they tell you) are very important to get right. Must prepare to know what you're going to do before class. Lab reports are due a week after which is nice. If you have Tommy Reason as your TA, you'll love the class! Albert himself is an easy grader.

analysis.name: Amy Pollock
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 206 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Amazing professor & very clear for those who may not understand chemistry well. Free book is a bonus. Very easy class. Participation and attendance required. Homework and recitation are "A for effort" grades. Short lectures. Fair amount of homework, but always short and easy. Easy tests if you study. If you did well in high school chem, you're fine

Amy is amazing. She is a super kind and a cute lady. However, if you do not come to the lectures, you will fail. Class material is basic chem and Amy teaches it super well. She is very passionate and explains every thing in great detail. There are about 2 easy homeworks a week.  Overall, if you come to class and pay attention, you should pass.

Dr. Pollock is a great professor and one of the best I've had at MSU. If you actually pay attention to the lectures then you will be fine. She makes chemistry easy to understand and a 4.0 is not very hard to get.

She is hands down one of the best professors that I ever had. The lectures were very easy to follow, but to understand the posted slides, you most often had to attend lecture. The exams tested your knowledge, but if you go and get outside help the exams are a piece of cake - and you can get extra credit. I would highly recommend her as a professor.

You need to attend lecture to understand anything, and then outside of lecture you need to look at the slides and make sure you understand what is going on. Study... a lot. The exams are nothing like what's done in lecture or recitation so make sure you look at the practice exams before hand and make sure you know how to do everything on them.

Dr. Brockey is a harsh grader make sure to read the fine print otherwise it will be a zero. No creative freedom with the essays.

Overall, he was very helpful and you can tell he cares deeply about his students.

Bob is a good professor, but he switches up. One day he likes you the next he is so rude to you. The projects are a lot outside of class, so make sure you have time for that. He also teaches and grades like this is a 400-level course even though it's the beginning of journalism for a lot of students. Does get frustrated easily. Overall, a 6/10.

Bob is a charming and funny guy, he sometimes likes to talk about fun things at the beginning of class, which created a very open and welcoming environment; everyone seemed comfortable talking. He kinda expects a lot from a 200 level class and might get frustrated if everyone missed something, but he is very helpful and accessible outside class.

Bob is very engaging and clearly cares about students' success. The projects and assignments may seem intimidating at first, but they are manageable if you stay organized and ask questions when needed. The class is well-structured, easy to follow, and enjoyable overall.

Bob Gould is one of the best professors I've had. He's a tough grader with high expectations, but if you participate and engage, the class is very enjoyable. His fun, goofy personality makes it interesting. The required video kit is expensive, but I would take this class again.

Got mad at class when everyone did bad on a question instead of realizing that the reason we did bad was because we never saw a question like that.

Class time felt wasted on things that had nothing to do with what we are learning. I learned absolutely nothing. Class is very easy and almost impossible to do badly if you just show up. The projects are straightforward, and the instructions are very clear, and gives you a ton of time to complete. Also very understanding and easy to reach.

analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Fun prof who cares about what he is teaching. Weekly homework and reading are posted, and the schedule stays the exact same throughout the entire semester. Can get hard/tedious with frequent hws, projects, and quizzes, but he's willing to extend deadlines/work with students.
He designed the course so he understands the material the best and dumbed it down so anyone can learn. Just like anything you need to put in the work.

Overall, Dr. Mason is a good professor. The amount of time given for the projects wasn't ideal, but it seems like Mason is adjusting the course to account for this. The lectures covered a lot of the same stuff from the textbook, which was a little strange. The homework was fair and the grading comments were always helpful in understanding mistakes.

HWs were graded by a few things. Sometimes the structure of his courses can be confusing. He is highly caring and the HWs are super well built to enhance your reading. He is a tough grader and his exams are very challenging, however, you build very good study habits from his classes as his structures promotes that. I'd also say he is inspirational.

Dr. Mason was an all-around great professor. The homework and design projects were a bit of a workload, but he gave you all of the material needed to excel in this course. While some people didn't find the required online textbook helpful, I believed that it was a great resource to have before starting a new chapter each week.

Professor Dixon probably ran the worst class of all time. Duke always brightened my day! He's super nice and funny! The workload could be a lot sometimes but make sure to communicate with him as he's pretty understanding and genuinely wants to see you succeed!!

I love Professor Duke. He's sweet, funny, and an incredible artist! Still, this class can be grueling (in-class still lifes & time consuming hw). Either way, I was able to get 100s on nearly all of my assignments. Show up so you can get your in-class hw credit (Iike fr) & you'll be fine. He's a really good guy, gives great critique and is an amazing artist himself. I feel like I improved. However, he's pretty scatterbrained, and sometimes has trouble managing a class. Expects you to work on each homework piece for a minimum of 6 hours, and attendance is mandatory. But he lets you wear headphones, so it's not too bad for drawing 1.

PROS: He's a nice guy, has a sense of humor He's a good artist. Lets you redo all assignments up until midterm (there is a HUGE but though.) CONS: EXTREMELY unclear grading criteria, Fairly large assignments due EVERY week. (the BUT... for the redoing assignments) Gives little feedback, what he does give is extremely cryptic.

review_highlights.comment: I'm not going to say much other than good luck to the chem majors (b/c there is no other option). You will need to memorize every small detail to do good on tests. The grading scale isn't clear. TA is great though.

She mumbles through lectures, skips class WITH ZERO WARNING, and gives absolutely no clear grading guideline. Tested on memorizing useless details. TA is literally fantastic.

The professor uses notes from Matthew D Law from UCL WORD FOR WORD. She does not elaborate beyond these PowerPoints. The exams expect you to MEMORIZE every small thing that was mentioned in lecture. This is not a learning based course. SHE DOES NOT USE A GRADING SCALE. The average determines a 3.0. The exam average was a 31%, making it a 3.0.

Dr. Demir is easily the worst teacher I've ever had. I have had more insightful bowl movements than this class was.

I had Dr. Acevedo last semester and she was definitely a favorite. She was very easy going, caring and the work was never anything stressful. If you face any sort of problem and just communicate she's almost always understanding. Little cornball but we love that for her :)

This class wasn't well structured, and it wasn't all Acevedo's fault. She's very caring, kind, and energetic, but the class activities, assignments, and projects weren't the best in my opinion. Attendance is mandatory, but she's a flexible and caring professor.

I have met no professors that match professor Rick's amazing positive energy and enthusiasm, with genuine care for his students! That's why I found CAS 111 class exciting to attend, on top of the already fun open-ended projects. It was one of my favorite classes at MSU, and the workload is moderate and fair. Great professor if you enjoy creativity.

tbf, this was a one credit class, but prof was so sweet and fun i loved him. this class was only for half of the semester and was just different adobe PS and Ai assignments that were pretty easy. only annoying thing that assignments were due at 5pm on tuesdays? he gave great feedback, answered emails, and made his video tuts very easy to understand

If you are not good with adobe do not take this class. The first few weeks of the class I cried on every assignment and spent hours doing it because it's so confusing. The professor is nice just chatty and hard grader. Overall, it gets easier as you learn more on adobe, but if you are looking for an easy elective this is not the class for you.

Can't say enough good things about Professor Rick. He's experienced in his field, gave great feedback, and really made an effort to get to know students in a large lecture hall. He even reached out to me personally to compliment my work. Took this class as an elective but enjoyed it a lot more than expected.

I just wish there would've been a clear study guide for exams.
She's awesome. A great person to talk to especially if you want advice on more career and education oriented stuff.

You will do well if you go to class and engage with the content. Dr. Pomeranz is a good professor and clarifies any confusion if you ask. I learned a lot in this class and enjoyed it!

Dr. Pomeranz completely lost the class a month in, maybe 25% came. Lectures are extremely boring and disorganized, you gain absolutely nothing from going. analysis.name: Edward Murphy
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He has done so many things with his life (which he will share), and he is extremely engaging to listen to. Be ready to do an extensive amount of reading. If you don't do readings, the class will be difficult for you. There are 4 "pop quizzes," but he always hints heavily at them. At first, you may not like him, but I promise he will grow on you!

IAH 203 is my favorite class this semester. Dr. Murphy is really funny and an engaging lecturer. The class is a lot of reading and there are some pop quizzes, but they are not hard. He's willing to answer questions after lectures. There are a couple essays, but as long as you follow the guidelines you will be fine. He's always been helpful to me :)

IAH 203 is SUPER reading heavy. I mean having 3-4 readings per week, each of which was at least 30 pages long. Don't try skipping them either, as they're just as important as in-class lectures. Each essay required at least 1 citation from three separate sources. Murphy was very passionate about the subject, making class lectures nice to attend

This course should be reviewed for the way grades are determined. One portion of the rubric highlights Attendance and Participation and details the required amount of participation for the course. This grade is discretionary, so the instructor is able to (and will) use a 30% chunk of the grade to give you the grade they want to give you.
One of the best professors you'll have. His ability to engage students with the material and lead thoughtful conversations is unmatched. He expects a lot from you, but you'll get out what you put in.

analysis.name: Kyle Evered
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently

His lower-level classes are very easy and are only exam based, while his higher level classes expect you to write a long paper. I would highly recommend anyone take GEO 440

GEO 214 was a pretty interesting class, but I attended 4 lectures at most. The class was fully graded off of 4 exams, and I found his lectures kind of boring despite the interesting basis of the class, personally it was because he got off-topic and I would just zone out. Got a 4.0 in the class because the exams were pretty straightforward.

Easiest class I've had in my entire life. It was actually pretty interesting and the professor is a really nice guy.  You could hypothetically not go to class at all and still take the 4 unproctored online exams that the class grade is based off of. Not to mention the tremendous amount of extra credit he gives. It's impossible to get a B.

Kyle is an amazing professor and I would venture to say he is one of the few professors that truly make MSU a great institution. From his lectures on Geopolitics, it was abundantly clear that he knew everything there was to know on the subject and truly delved deep into topics rather than just providing an overview of the subject.

Extremely good at teaching and explains everything so well! Definitely recommend taking his class.

Grade is based off of only 2 quizzes, midterm, final, and paper.

analysis.name: Bethany Furqueron

She is so knowledgeable of the material and made sure everyone had a clear understanding of the content for the exams. Her lectures were engaging with group work. She is just a caring, encouraging person. Definitely one of the best professors I've had so far.

She makes the lectures super interesting, which cannot be said about most professors. She cares if you understand the material and is super helpful when it comes to questions. It is very easy to get points off on all of the assignments in here but overall she is an amazing professor.
Super amazing class would take agian.
Dr. Furqueron is quite actually the best instructor I have ever had! Her class is set up in a way where you really learn the material and it's enjoyable to go to class!!!!!!

analysis.name: Florencia Rojo

review_highlights.comment: Do not take this class! Not good at all with communication and passive aggressive when communicating. You have to print out every reading, so when it's 60 pages, it's extremely expensive. I practically went into debt printing her assignments.

All expectations were so unclear and if asked about them, she would be passive aggressive and borderline offended. So much reading and you will not go over majority of it, unfortunately felt like a waste of time/money. Had all scholars of color last and were given less attention than non POC scholars. Hates teaching undergrad and it shows. AVOID!!!

Extremely vague and unclear with assignment directions, which made it hard to know what was expected. Responses to questions often came off as passive-aggressive, and the feedback provided was not helpful or constructive. The course also required printing a large amount of material, which ended up costing a lot of money throughout the semester.

She has a power trip that reaches an extremely unprofessional level. Her instructions are often unclear, and she becomes frustrated when students do not understand her vague guidance. She dislikes having to “repeat herself,” even though the information she claims to be repeating is not included in the syllabus or clearly addressed in lectures.

DO NOT TAKE HER. Terrible person. Does not answer questions in emails. "it's on the syllabus" bs. ONLY HAS ONE DAY OF OFFICE HOURS?? If you ask a question on an email she'll send a class announcement acting as if answering questions is not her job. Terrible essay feedback. Has a superiority complex against her students?? ruined my gpa; avoiding her

Specifically, rubrics had word counts for specific paragraphs, and she would walk around the lecture to make sure you were paying attention and didn't have your laptop out were some things that really pissed me off. She brought valuable information to class but I felt  like I was in 6th grade

Flaim is nice, and passionate. She cares for her students and her cause. However, she frequently goes off topic, which stops you from getting answers to your questions. She also grades harder than the other professors so you will probably have to work harder than your fellow classmates.
She is very understanding towards students and is passionate about her teaching.

Tough grader, all readings are similar and not interesting. The class is tailored for specific people. It is unorganized and good luck getting a 4.0 on a paper. Her grading makes absolutely no sense. Would not wish this on my worst enemy

analysis.name: Chuck Fessler

review_highlights.comment: Whatever you do, do not take this class. He changes the way you're graded constantly and literally cannot teach. If you are not already a master at trig, STAY AWAY. He overcomplicates everything and will take points away if you don't do work the way he wants it. He's actually a pretty nice guy, but worst prof I've ever had.

HORRIBLE class. He is a nice guy but I dont think teaching math is his thing. take calculus through university you get online exams.  if you don't want to watch your grade drop every week take it outside. really bad grading his teaching style is also wack.  the exam study guide doesn't correlate with the exam. Nice guy needs to consider changing su

Actually a horrendous professor (nice guy though). Ended up teaching myself everything because of it. Study guides do not help, and a very misleading grading system. You will have quizzes every week (on and off independent and group style) in recitation which is required. You cannot skip these quizzes without a doctor's note (same for exams).

Very passive-aggressive when asking questions, almost rude even. Not good at teaching and with the most unclear grading criteria possible. I legit couldn't see my percent grade all semester. Expect lots of meaningless group projects and busy work. Weekly quizzes that are pretty easy, but oftentimes hard to understand. Do not take.

I took LB 117 online, for the most part it was the same content as my high school calculus class but he either never elaborated on what he wanted us to do on the labs, or briefly went over what material he wanted us to turn in and always took so long to grade stuff. Overall horrible experience.

analysis.name: Nicholas Fields
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This professor is such a fantastic, knowledgeable lecturer who has a deep passion for the topic. He explains these topics so well and with such excitement, it gets me excited to learn. I learned so much from this class without it being difficult.
Very nice guy that seems to care a lot about his students. Easy and fun class to take, good elective.

I took this class very last minute not knowing anything at all about music. One of the best professors I have ever had so far at MSU. He is really engaging and cares that you pass. Not even a music major! I am business but was my favorite class this semester.

He made the classroom a fun environment, and was very understanding near the end of the semester. His grading is very relaxed and the weekly assignment was a paragraph on whatever I wanted. I really enjoyed understanding music i'm gonna miss that guy

It wouldn't let me choose the correct course but I took IAH 241a with Professor Fields, which was Music and Society in the Modern World. I loved this class, especially for an IAH. Prof Fields has such a caring, kind demeanor about him which made me want to participate even more. Easy workload as well. This was the way an IAH course SHOULD be.

analysis.name: Camille Fairbourn
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Sweetest prof. ever, poor teaching style. Made many mistakes, not tech-savvy, wasted time. Wanted us to succeed, helpful 1-on-1 but should be teaching a smaller class. Content shouldn't have seemed so dificult to understand, I didn't like the way she overcomplicated things/underexplained things. She deserves to teach a subject she's better at

Professor Fairbourn genuinely made me like a math class! She is so kind and answers any questions! One homework assignment per week, 2.5% added to your final grade if you do all the EC, my TA was amazing and helped me understand the content. The Stats Learning Center is such an amazing resource if you're struggling, I highly recommend utilizing it!

Prof Fairborn seems like a sweet woman but it almost felt like she knew too much for a base level stats class, it got confusing at times. She goes through slides fast and it was hard to keep up during lectures. If you feel confident about math you'll be fine. If you struggle with math, then you may want to make sure you can find outside help.

Lectures and recitations were quite confusing. I thought that the lectures were a bit all over the place, and it was hard for me to follow what we were learning. She is really nice, but I do not think that she is the best teacher and I found the course difficult due to her teaching style.

I would try to take another professor. She makes the lectures very confusing, and most of the time, you are just doing examples and not actually learning the content, which made me have to learn it outside of class. Attendance is mandatory, but she offers make-up attendance questions at the beginning of the week. I wouldn't retake it.

analysis.name: George Harnick
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 27 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Love this guy! The class was very easy, and there were only 4 assignments the whole time. Guys, please laugh at his joke of the day it makes me sad when people don't! Kinda quirky, but a very passionate teacher and someone who would help you in the future in a heartbeat.
Such an amazing professor! Genuinely made every lecture so engaging and enjoyable. He is so funny and goes out of his way to accommodate and help students, could not recommend him enough!!

My favorite professor by far! He truly cares, adds humor to keep lectures engaging, makes students comfortable asking questions, and is always responsive to emails, even if you're a former student. He truly helped me love the class and want to be there and engaged. You have to write your name on a piece of paper when you go, but it's not mandatory.
The most understanding and personalble professor.

George is one of my absolute favorite professors. Super engaging with the students and genuinely cares about his students' learning. You'll have to study for his exams but nothing too difficult. Also a little bit of homework but totally managable

analysis.name: Gabriel Nagy

review_highlights.comment: As course coordinator, I thought his weekly quizzes were rough since they have the same number of questions as the exams, and the exams also cover old material which was annoying (exam 3 covers material from exams 1 and 2). While he was very organized and never missed a single lecture, his teaching style is like an AI chatbot. He only describes the same basic overviews of course topics over and over again and rarely shows the class how to solve problems that may appear on exams and WebWork. He is way too broad in his explanation of things and expects a lot.

If you are coming in as a freshman and did not do any math over the summer do not take this class. He does have an accent but which can make it hard to understand him sometimes but if you focus you can understand him decently but the main problem is that he does not explain things well at all, he just does the math and kinda moved on right away

The professor himself is nice however the teaching is kind fof bad. He basically records his hand written notes (not like MacCombs he actually handwrites them) and all the videos are an hour long. But it takes you 2-3 hours PER video (3 times a week) to actually even write it down not understand it because he prefills and then reads right off it.

analysis.name: Gerald Urquhart

While the grading guidelines were VERY forgiving and allow almost unlimited retakes, Urquhart is just a bit confusing to understand when it comes to lecture as he always seems a little confused/lost. Poor guy is also very stressed out. Otherwise he's a great professor and teaches very interesting material!

Dr. Urquhart is awesome!!! He teaches exactly enough to make you understand, just go to class and pay attention. He lets students (like me) work on special projects with him outside of class, and even has class field trips!!! 4.0'd the class easy. Just beware of 155's chem portion.
Great professor!  Really loves the content he teaches and has a passion for it. He was always understanding of circumstances and gave clear criteria of what was expected of his students.

I did not have him as a professor although I turned to him for help as he is the assistant dean of lyman briggs. He offers amazing help. analysis.name: Sharon Griffin

Griffin is nice and approachable, but she moves quickly through lectures. She speaks fast and only leaves notes on the screen for 15 seconds. I would definitely recommend Allen.

I would do everything to get out of this course. Reads off Powerpoint slides, exams are easy, same for homework and quizzes, Iclicker grade

Overall an okay professor.

The prerequisite for this course is calc I, yet we were expected to know and apply several calc II topics to the lecture homework. The labs are helpful but the lecture was a HUGE waste of time. Gives very tedious busy work. The exams are only 4 questions but you'll be lucky to get to the last problem. One of the worst profs I've had at MSU.

Your group is assigned by alphabet order, four people to a group. You can skip, but your attendance is noted. Handle yourself professionally, act in a professional manner, and you should be fine. Harsh Grader, takes weeks to get our test back STAY AWAY FROM THIS PROFESSOR

Professor Hoffman is amazing! He has amazing lectures and assignments that are really fun to do. He defiantly helps you see things in a new light. So much busy work, for no reason. Tough grader, even when an assignment is fully completed.

He did genuinely nothing at all. The class was extremely confusing and he made it so bad. Listen to me. This man is one of the nicest guys, but if you are not passionate about political science, save urself and don't take this class.

analysis.name: Helen Veit

review_highlights.comment: The exams were cumulative with no study guide and no narrowing of topics. We had to reference readings and lectures in projects and exams without looking back on notes. Professor Veit is a great professor but the ways she structures the class is stupid. The GPA Requirement to get a 4.0 is 94% which is already high paired with the fact that you have 7 Unit Exams and a Final it's quite hard to get a 4 unless you get an A on every exam. The final is also cumulative of all 7 units and you aren't given a study guide.

Prof Veit is one of the best professors at MSU. Expectations are clear and easy to follow. There's a strict no-tech policy in class, and although it may seem strange, it was super beneficial. She is very passionate about what she does, and I would encourage everyone to take her class. Exams and quizzes are VERY easy as long as you pay attention.

Best professor I've had at MSU. The class is difficult, but isn't that the point of an upper-level course? She's a fair grader, gives amazing feedback, and pushes everyone to be better. I came out of this class a better student & greatly improved my ability to think and read. Highly, highly recommend Dr Veit.

Dr. Viet is a great professor and also easily accessible, she has office hours right after class. analysis.name: Heather Eisthen

Difficult to receive helpful feedback due to her rude manners. Unable to ask questions in class without a snarky remark. Pulls the most niche/hard topics from lectures to use on the exams. She is clearly very passionate about this subject and I found the lectures very interesting and useful. This class was fairly hard, but I really enjoyed it. She talks really fast but is really receptive to feedback and if she needs to slow down. She's super sarcastic which I think can come across as rude but whenever I met with her one-on-one she was super helpful and wanted us to learn the material.

I took his class based on the reviews here and he is a good teacher but he is kind of a dictator in the class. He gives lots of reading and you have to be ready for class discussions, the first exam was easy but the ones after that were hard. All I can say is keep up with the readings and GO to class most of the exams are from class discussion.

I was so surprised to see negative reviews on Dr. Hourani. He was truly one of my favorite professors, and while his classes are reading heavy, he is very patient and understanding. If you make an effort and have open communication with him about any problems, you will do well in this class. He is engaging and makes the class feel connected.

analysis.name: Harish Sankaranarayanan

He gives super boring lectures, really wants you to switch to econ a a major (which i never will). Also mandatory quizzes every class for attedance. But tbh you can just pay attention during the review sessions and he gives you thr awnser to like 80% of the exam. Just study those

analysis.name: Kirk Kraetzer
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty

review_highlights.comment: Dr. HK is one of my favorite professors. He is so funny and easy to talk to. He is very caring and is willing to work with you if you need help or accommodations. His grading is a little confusing but its not that difficult to do well in the class if you follow directions and ask questions.

Kirk's class is very interesting. I was genuinely intrigued at every lecture, and all of his assignments were meaningful. It was a decent amount of work, but if you put in the effort you will exceed. He is very helpful with feedback and does a great job teaching. He is very intelligent and is passionate about what he talks about. I would recommend!

I was hesitant about this class at first because it seemed like a lot of work, and it was, but I genuinely felt that every assignment was meaningful. Kirk's class taught me so much and I still think about it everyday. I loved his teaching style and he is very intelligent. He was also super helpful! I would definitely recommend his class!

Everything Dr. Kraetzer assigned, you had a chance to revise if it didnt meet the expectations set in the rubric. The rubrics were very straightforward. It was very easy to get a 4.0 in this class because you could revise literally everything. He also gave in-depth feedback on everything, so it was super easy to revise if needed.

LB133 was very boring and long, however it was made tolerable and even fun at times because of the way prof. Kraetzer teaches. He is passionate about what he talks about and how he talks about it. This class is very easy and it's pretty easy to 4.0, he can be a little unclear with what exactly he wants, but if you put in effort, you'll be fine.

analysis.name: Kristine Rose
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Such a pleasure having her as a professor for my first and last year as a nursing student. The sweetest lady and she genuinely cares about your success. If you are struggling in her class, meet with her and she will give you tips that you will carry on for the rest of nursing school. The best professor I've ever had!

Dr. Rose truly cares about her students' success and well-being. I learned so much foundational knowledge in her pathophysiology class. Her lectures are engaging, and she finds the perfect balance of words and visuals on the slide and interesting stories from her experience as a nurse that help you remember the material.

Dr. Rose is THE BEST professor I've ever had. She makes class interesting, and she gives you examples of possible exam questions during lecture. Not a lot of homework for the course, however, you will need to study if you want to do well! She is very understanding and wants all students to succeed. 10/10 would recommend & I hope to have her again!

One of the best professors I've ever had. I get easily distracted during lectures but I would hang on every word she said. She tells interesting stories that actually relate back to the material. Extremely kind and funny lady.
Really sweet and constantly brings in stories to connect with the lecture that shes teaching. Would love to have her again!

analysis.name: Ryan Kimbirauskas
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 82 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr.K is so caring and funny and he has really helpful lectures. Attendance isn't mandatory, but sometimes there's a pop quiz. I think it's really important to show up as much as you can anyway. The lectures he gives are pretty much exactly what you're going to see on the exams, and he makes it all very straightforward as long as you pay attention.

Dr. K is the best professor you could have for an 8am lecture. He cares so much about his students and loves it when you engage. His lectures were interesting and you can tell he is passionate about what he teaches.

Doctor Kimbirauskas has been my favorite professor at MSU yet. He expects a lot from his students, and pop quizzes can be assigned, however, he is very accessible and make the topics discussed super interesting. I learned so much from this class and I was only really taking it to complete my ISB credit. Awesome professor.

Loved this class! Professor was really engaging and had some funny sotries to share. Even though the class was exam heavy it really isnt hard to get a 4.0 in this class. I did'nt really pay attention in class and studied for maybe two hours for each exam and always got above a 95%. Theres also plenty of extra credit. Only had 2 pop quizzes!!!

The exams are difficult, no study preparation material, only resources include "looking back" at lecture slides. When Dr. K was asked how to improve grade in the class, he said "look back at the slides and THINK ABOUT IT." MCQ format is difficult with options such as A,B,C,D,AB,BC,CA,All of the above. 
Good guy in general, just not a good prof.

analysis.name: Katherine Krueger
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: The was no teaching that occurred in the lecture and most of it was groupwork. Most of the time the groups are lost on the clicker assignment and the ULAs don't do a great job on clarifying the doubts. The pre-lecture videos are somewhat disconnected to what happens in the lecture and it is frustrating.

Suuuper sweet professor, she learns almost everyone's names! Super kind and will sit with you till you understand. She is also super open for any questions and work you need help with! The only thing is the class is structured really weird... definitely not a lot of fun, a LOT of homework, and 70% of it is work you have to do on your own.

She is sweet but I HATE how this class is a flipped course. Honestly believe if it was like a regular lecture, many would know what the heck is going on in class. The pre class activities are understandable but the in class activities are confusing. Quizzes every Monday from last weeks units. Every assignment is graded on accuracy and completion

This is a flipped learning class, meaning that you will need to watch all of her pre-class videos before doing un-graded group busy work in class. I think the flipped learning structure is un-helpful, and I found her video explanations weren't good

She is honestly super sweet and likes to engage with her class. there is a-lot of bust work to prepare before class and you are expected to know it for the in class activity and quizzes that are every day. I learned a-lot overall though! do not skip class

analysis.name: James Lambert
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: Cool and knowledgeable teacher, be ready for a very BORING lecture. I think this is more so on the class but its slow and boring. Quizzes and exams are easy asf, can fade 4 classes. Gives pop quizzes (16 of them, 12 are graded) but you can fade. I faded probably 10 times and still easily passed without reading once. Writing assignments are light.

Overall the class was easy to complete. He is very lecture heavy but does allow for discussion. Attendence was not mandatory but there are assignments asked during class and he gives 16 (12 in grade book) so you can miss 4 quizzes w/out penalty Recitation is required (can miss 3x). Perfers hand written notes he does not like tech. boring but easy

Most boring and Un-useful class I've ever taken. If you need an IAH don't take this unless u love philosophy. So heavy philosophy based it's insane. All he does is yap about the readings he assigned. A lot of reading and a lot of written assessments based off them. You have to go to the class to get credit. Not a hard, just strange and boring 2/10!

Amazing Professor. In my first semester of college, I enjoyed his class the most by far. I wasn't always focused, and it was okay; he and his TAs were there to help whenever needed. Doesn't take attendance, but we had random pop quizzes, and as long as you did them, you basically got a 4.0. Very kind and accommodating to anything you might need.

I really enjoyed Dr. Lambert's class. Dr. Lambert is very passionate about his feminist views, so if you share those views take this class. If you don't, do not. He assigns readings and holds discussions about them in class, so make sure you do the readings and participate in discussion. A few very short written assignments and no exams.

analysis.name: Lucy Thompson
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Thompson is fantastic, she is so kind, knowledgable and accessible outside of class. You do not necessarily need to go to class, but it certainly helps! a really great prof! A lot of drops which is really nice, but if you don't want to go to class I would get the book or vise versa. However I will say it is so lecture heavy and I did have to fight my sleep demons more times then I would like LOL. I do wish there were more discussions and more diverse voices and opinions were heard.

Ms. Thompson's class was very lecture-heavy. I often felt bored and overwhelmed trying to copy each slide before she moved on. The nearly two-hour lectures were tiring, and the exams every two to three weeks were all memorization-based. The homework was simple—two short quizzes and an assignment every week.
Dr. Thompson is sweet, and her lectures are inspiring and straightforward. Attendence was not mandatory. The exams were harder than I expected, but she allows multiple drops.

Dr. Thompson was nice and had interesting stories sometimes but her whole lecture was reading directly off of slides. If you are able to read through textbooks and make quizlets to learn rather than note taking I would recommend this class but it was not enjoyable and I was often stressed about writing everything down as she clicked through slides.

analysis.name: Kevin Walker
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 82 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Would not recommend any one to take cem 251 with Dr. Walker. I feel that he assumes his students know what he is talking about when in reality we are all clueless. He poorly explains topics and claims that his practice problems are far more difficult than his exam problems which is completely untrue. If you're not pre-med or pre-vet, run away.

DO NOT TAKE ORGANIC CHEMISTRY WITH DR. WALKER! He is a terrible teacher, and doesn't seem to care if the students learn the material. He's rather rude and will make you feel dumb if you don't know the answer to questions he asks. His exams are outrageous. This is the worst experience I've had at MSU.

Dr. Walker is a very intelligent man; however, he does not understand how to teach his knowledge to those who have never seen organic chemistry before. Choose other professors to learn the material, because he talks more about trying to make students understand him than actually presenting the material to his students in a way that's easy to grasp.

Do not take CEM 251 with walker. I learned more from the TAs/tutors and by teaching myself than he ever taught me. His lectures are hardly worth it. He does not know how to teach effectively and he constantly jumps all over the place. Hes a nice guy, but could use some guidance on how to teach.

I think his low rating is unwarranted. Mr. Walker is an expert in what he teaches and if you learn through analogy or stories then he will be a great professor. I would understand if his teaching style wasn't for everyone, but lectures are not going to be boring at least. Just attend lectures, study, review: I found outlining the textbook helpful.

analysis.name: Marilyn   Wulfekuhler

this class is horrible. TA's never go over quizzes so if u didn't know what u were doing, u still won't! everyones reviews talking about academic dishonesty and cheating are true. No wonder the CSE requirement was dropped for the business school because the course is so poorly taught I hope the professor is fired

This was such a hard class for being a introductory. If you love yourself, don't take this class. for ece 410, the longest project i have ever had to do was this class. the professor does not help and grades extremely tough and does not help at all

Professor Wake was an amazing professor. Her lectures were extremely clear and the semester expectations were laid out from the beginning of the semester. Dr. Wake is compassionate and completely no-nonsense. Show up, do worksheet, collect A. It's that simple.

Professor Wake's class was one of my favorites I have ever taken. Her lectures were super interesting and I learned so much from the class. The readings are important but they're never very long. I took her class as I heard there was not a textbook but ended up likeing finance a lot more than I can ever imagine. She gave a lot of flexibilities and really cared for her students to succeed. I am good with computer stuff so the class is a lot easier for me than my friends. Remember it's a finance class.

I recommend that everyone take this class! It's such a good class when you just need a few extra credits but don't want something difficult. Your grade is entirely based off of quizzes and tests but as long as you look over the lectures they are super easy. He makes the class very enjoyable and writes the nicest emails every week!

Honestly, an amazing professor. He's fully online and just has quizzes throughout the week that you have like a month to complete. I didn't even have to take the final because he only makes you keep 3 of the exams out of the 4. Also a really funny guy.

Great professor and a great class. Surprisingly interesting, and the professor is very nice and wants his students to do good. Despite being fully online, the class is well organized and easy to keep up with as well. Definitely recommend!

analysis.name: Paul Nelson

I wouldn't take this class again. This capstone class is not very helpful in my opinion. The labor based grading system is very flawed as well. If you have to take this class, good luck. Also be prepared for tons of busy work every week, including the week of spring break.

Good professor. Bald professor. Interacts with students. Project based class: One group project and on individual project. Weekly quizzes. Interesting grading system, but there are extra credit opportunities.

Awful class. For 98% of people it is a required class that is so obnoxiously hard. Very direct and can have an attitude. Classes consist of mostly answering HW questions, which wasn't helpful as little time was left for lecture slides. Seems like a nice person, but I find the class to be mind-numbing. Expect to learn the material on your own time because the whole class time is taken up reviewing the homework from the day before.

This professor does not help you learn anything. She instead uses her time to send multiple emails out to students accusing them of using AI.
