analysis.name: Olufunmbi Elemo
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment:
MC377: Culture, Politics, and Postcolonialism: Profiling Sub-Saharan Africa
Here's the tea: Elemo is VERY supportive in providing resources and suggestions for final projects and large essays. Has engaging lectures and values class participation. Communication is key, highly recommend attending office hours. E-K is a great prof for this subject.

I had Professor Elemo for MC 201 and am currently taking her MC 492 class. She does an excellent job explaining complex readings and breaking them down clearly. She is thoughtful, supportive, and genuinely cares about her students' success.

Professor Elemo's truly one of my favorite JMC professors. I had some medical issues towards the end of the semester and she was extremely understanding when it came to my absences (unlike some other professors). She's truly passionate about what she's teaching and talking to her about class material is extremely beneficial. Highly recommend!

I had her for MC 201. Though I didn't like her class my freshman year, I realized she's actually an amazing professor in MC325! She has amazing lectures, helpful during office hours, and overall a very understanding professor if you show up. Attendance is very important but you're allowed four absences which is much more than other professors.

Contrary to popular belief, she's a very good prof. Her tone may be condescending at times, but she teaches well and has clear expectations. She is a tough grader but provides good advice. Just take her feedback into account and go to office hours if you're struggling and you'll be fine.

analysis.name: Orlando Hawkins
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: My favorite JMC prof I've had thus far, he creates a comfy environment. I used to be so nervous to join discussions, but I was good to share my takes in this class. He gives genuine feedback, and will happily meet with you if you need help. He also lectures with slides instead of just yapping for a straight hour and a half. Pls take him he's great.

Professor Hawkins is a refreshing change in the PTCD lineup. He has moved away from the usual Straussian dogma toward a more critical, historically grounded approach. If you're a Straussian, you may not enjoy the critical readings so much, but there will be ample opportunity to interpret and grapple with the canonical texts. Participating is key!

Professor Hawkins is brand new to JMC/PTCD, but he is a truly great teacher. He really impressed me, and he did not shy away from tough topics, and fairly presented all the reasonable angles in this class, which is a pretty controversial class. I Highly, HIGHLY reccomend taking classes with him.

analysis.name: Maximilien Peroux
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Peroux is an effective and accommodating teacher, but the course content is challenging. Expect weekly quizzes with the material. If you attend class, pay attention, and complete the work, you will pass. Homework and attendance aren't mandatory, but in-class assignments and quizzes are required. Good teacher, bad course. Would take again.

Péroux is super nice and caring. The class is set up in a way that there is a quiz or two every week, but we get 3 shots for each graded objective. The system is set up so that there is a lot of work for us students, but the professor is doing a great job with what is given.

I took Péroux's class thinking it'd be just another credit, but I ended up rethinking my whole relationship to math. He has a way of explaining difficult ideas with elegance and patience. His French accent adds to the charm, he's articulate and thoughtful. I walked out of this class more confident, curious, and inspired than I've ever been in STEM.

I really enjoy going to his lectures. He goes over everything carefully and always allows us to ask questions. I cannot understand the lecture videos by the others, but Prof. Peroux always make things super clear. Sometimes he goes a bit slowly on some examples, but it helps me really understand what is going on.

Amazing instructor. He was proctoring an exam for my class and handled everything with professionalism and kindness, which really helped me stay focused. I attended his lecture afterward and his explanations were incredibly clear and easy to follow. Highly recommend.

analysis.name: Matthew Pauly
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: openly admitted we were going to skip things he felt were over taught because he finds them boring and would rather teach about his favorite parts of ww2. we only receive 4 grades 3 exams with vague prompts that require exact citations from 500+ pages of readings and participation.  please take another class and don't ruin a semester.

This was HST 344 Causes and Conflicts of WW2 but he said the European conflicts are over taught and decided to spend almost the entire class talking about  the USSR. we were assigned 100+ pages of reading most weeks and he refused to post his slides. We were only graded on 4 things all semester. Pleas don't take this class.

this class is just his personal project and not close to the course description offered by MSU. if you enjoy hearing about the glory of the Soviet Union this is the class for you. if you want to learn about the rest of the war find another professor. graded on 3 exams and participation only.

will mark exams down for misspellings, and then takes 5-6 weeks to return exams. were assigned 4 books to read at the same time and have over 100 pages to read between classes. if you value your gpa and sanity I recommend finding another class.
He does not know how to lecture, and goes on many tangents. never taking a class with him again.

analysis.name: Peter Thompson
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I took IAH 206. He is absolutely amazing. Didn't think I'd be interested in the class, but his teaching style and voice make the lectures fly by. Definitely lecture-heavy, but he recognizes that and tries his best to include participation. Tests were extremely fair and easy. Cares about his curriculum and his students. highly recommend taking!

Incredible professor and super interesting class. Heavily focused on readings and discussions, but you can complete them whenever you get a chance and still get credit. Super fun guy and the lectures were interesting, engaging, and I never wanted to skip. Exams are open note, and there's only one essay assignment. I recommend this class to everyone

This class was truly fascinating and could not have been made better. Although the readings were sometimes a lot, Dr. Thompson was very lenient and allowed us to make up missed discussions on our own time without penalty. I couldn't recommend this class more, regardless of your major.

One of the best professors I have ever had. Truley cares about the students. Has thought provoking assignments and interesting field trips. Lectures can be mundane, but they rarely are and take up a small portion of the class. Could not recommend his class enough.

Dr Thompson is an incredible professor. His lectures are super interesting, and his assignments and field trips are really fun and interactive. He is also extremely understanding and cares about the well being of his students above all, and is just an amazing instructor overall. I would 100% take this class again!

analysis.name: Osvaldo Hernandez
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 52 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: You think that you understand the material, you study the study guides he gives you, then you get the exam and are mind blown because it is nothing like you expected! Super hard exams that is for sure. Really boring lectures, too. Randomly gives in class work for credit so you should definitely go to lecture.

Such a nice professor!!! You also can tell how much he loves teaching this. Made class interesting enough for people who don't like science. Group projects that weren't awful although some days were more boring than others. Mandatory attendance but he usually lets us go early.

Lectures were boring as I'm not passionate about the environment, but Ozzy is a caring professor and an interesting person. Attendance is based on short questions you have to turn in online after class, and exams were online for the winter/spring '25 semester. He understands outside circumstances and will be lenient as long as you have reason.
The TAs teach the course. I've never even met the main professor. If you get a good TA, then you will get a good grade. Luckily, mine was amazing!

In class assignments you can do from home, lectures are SO hard to sit through. three exams that were all taken online outside of class, not proctored. I would recommend to others for integrative studies requirement. very easy coursework that takes less than 10 mins. not a lot of homework at all

analysis.name: Laura Jones- Pettit
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Very understanding. As long as you show up to class regularly, she is lenient about accepting late assignments.

I had her online section of writing and she lays out the class beautifully and it is so easy to get a good grade if you just do the work. She is very kind and understanding and such an amazing teacher I wish I could have her as a professor again!

Any preconceived notions had about a writing class, throw them out the window. All the projects are very fun and/or manageable, she gives you ample amounts of time to complete them, has very engaging lectures, and gives good feedback on competed projects. Also a very likeable professor in general.
She is easily my favorite professor so far. She is really dedicated to supporting her students and seeing them succeed, and gives excellent feedback on your writing to guide you.

I never write reviews like this, but for Professor Jones I have to! She is one of my favorite Profs ever!!! Her WRA101 class consists of 5 projects and as long as you complete them, put in genuine effort and follow the rubric you will receive an A. Would take a million times again! Such a sweet woman too- she really really cares about her students!

analysis.name: Lee Penyak
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: For a normal IAH requirement this class was insane. I spent most of my free time on this homework. Sometimes the homework did not relate to class content at all and everything was graded by AI so he couldn't explain why sometimes you would get a lower grade. His lectures would go in circles and test questions were just so specific and picky.

Dr. Penyak was delightful and you can see how much passion he has for this class through his lectures. He grades generally easy and while there is a lot of information to memorize for the tests, the tests themselves are very easy to pass and he applies a generous curve to each exam. His love for history makes the course very engaging.
dr. penyak was amazing!! when i didn't do so good on the first exam, he reached out to me first and invited me to office hours. he is really good at keeping the class engaged, too.
dr. penyak was amazing. when i didn't do so good on the first exam, he reached out first and invited me to office hours. his lectures kept me engaged, too.

Very interesting class, Professor is very knowledgeable on Mexican history with personal connections. Daily discussion posts that once you understand what he wants are easy to get good grades on. The tests aren't too hard, he also gave an extra credit. I would definitely take a class with him again.

analysis.name: Amber Peters
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 28 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: To be honest her class is pretty easy. There are in class questions you must answer for attendance/grade, but class material is pretty easy. Exams are half multiple choice half written but again not hard. She is gone doing research a lot so will have canceled classes/ TA ran classes which is nice. My downfall was not paying attention in class

Dr. Peters is super nice! She taught half of the lectures, and Dr. Peacor taught the other half. I think that she had simpler topics, so it was easier to understand her. The rest of the class was quite difficult outside of her lectures. Something that made things a bit difficult was her lack of study materials for exams.

Dr. Peters is a great professor! She obviously knows what she's talking about and welcomes any questions or comments on the material. She makes an effort to get to know the class and lectures are engaging and interesting. Attendance is not required but participation matters! Exams are written response but easy if you go to class and participate.

I loved Dr. Peters! I enjoyed taking her Great Lakes Bio class. It wasn't a ton of work and the quizzes felt fair. This semester, she offered that if you had over a 90% in the class you didn't have to take the final exam so make sure you attend class! There were no attendance drops but a few chances for extra credit.

Dr. Peters is a good professor and she is obviously very knowledgeable in her field. However, her grading is weird sometimes and her quizzes/tests are all short answer. I would take her class again, but be prepared for it to be slightly unorganized and for her to be gone several lectures.

analysis.name: lLina Qu
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: easy and super interesting class that only meets once a week. Just gotta go to class and raise your hand 6 times in a semester for full participation so easy again. Readings are through perusall which is annoying but again if you can't read 20 pages once a week you probably should not be in college. a few easy cooking assignments, great prof.

The class literally isn't that hard. Some of these reviews are just overreacting. That being said, I wouldn't take the class if you aren't into East Asia, which I feel like is pretty obvious already. There is only one lecture every week and one quiz every week with some projects and you need to participate 10 total times in class for the whole sem.

There is a weekly quiz on a movie and/or a reading every week which can be annoying. There are participation stickers and you need 10 to get 100%. Attendance is mandatory with two unexcused. Quizzes are not lock down. Has a midterm paper and final online presentation. Nice teacher, didn't have any problems.

Loved Dr. Qu! I'm honestly not sure why these reviews are so bad… her class is extremely easy. I got stuck with this class because it was the only IAH that fit into my schedule, however, I really enjoyed it. Class was only once a week and I actually found the lectures to be pretty interesting. Easy homework (quizzes) and midterm/final assignments.

Read the weekly course material and participate in class- the course is easy. People love to complain about everything. If you put effort into the essay portion of quiz you'll earn extra credit; I had no problems. 

I recommend this class to anyone genuinely interested in East Asia, b/c I enjoyed the material she provided. The lectures are boring.

analysis.name: Shannon Quinn
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Lessons cover a lot of the class prep activities relating to the shows watched in class this semester. Very flexible with submitting late work and she if she doesn't allow corrections on summary activities (tests), they're usually given a bit of a curve anyway. Я люблю Жанну :)
If you can take her for Russian, do! She's a great professor and is very generous. It's Russian, so you're going to have to work, but as long as you keep up you'll do fine.

Shannon is very kind and understanding, very flexible with late work as well, which is good considering the heavy workload for Russian. She's also pretty funny. Love hearing about the babushka lore. Lessons follow the Mezdhu Nami workbook until it's finished, then they go onto prep for the spring semester of 200 level RUS

The professor is nice, but this class is so boring. You have online prep videos, reading assignments, and a reading quiz all twice a week. We had two creative writing assignments and a final. Stories are originally in Russian and translated, so they don't make much sense and are very long and boring. Take another class if you can

If you have any other options, do not take this class. There is pre class work for every class, a reading assignment with questions, a quiz, and an online prep. It sounds easy but it's very time consuming. She will give pre class work the same days we have projects or writing assignments due. The lectures are very boring and just all her opinions.

analysis.name: Qiben Yan
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: He has a class policy of requesting an extension by 10pm. Me and my friend both missed the deadline but just to try our luck, we both emailed him. My friend got an extension while I didn't. How do you explain that!
Took the slides and homework from the the professor who taught the class in the previous semester, changed his name and that's it! He doesn't care if you understand. However, easy exams!
Worst lecturer. Too strong an accent, can't comprehend what he is saying. He comes to the class, talks to himself for 80mins and leaves.

analysis.name: Adan Quan
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Let Professor Quan know if you use or plan to use AI, or your grade will be affected. The material was a bit outdated and relied heavily on articles and external sources, followed by multiple small quizzes, a discussion, and an exam. While reading-heavy, it was an easy A (exams are heavily based on the external sources and articles).

As this class is an online class, I can't say much about the professor but more on the course. I really enjoyed this class and was really interested that I actually want this class to be made in person as well. The downside is that there are a lot of reading to do and wish that it could be summarized down a bit.

I took ANP 429 and it was a very enjoyable and memorable experience. Class is friendly to beginner ethnographers and the professor is caring towards your progress. The readings are not overwhelming by any means and the class structures you well for the final project. Amazing professor with a lot of experience and knowledge in the field.

He is very cautious about plaigarism/ChatGPT so be careful. However the class itself was super easy. You just have to read quite a bit and write discussion posts and take some small quizzes. Thats really it though

Prof Quan has interesting material however there is so much reading and additional articles that it was unrealistic for me to actually process the content even though I was genuinely interested and wanted to learn. If he cut out the excess requirements I would have had a much deeper understanding of everything we covered.

analysis.name: Simei Qing
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I feel bad giving her a lower rating because she is very sweet and kind to all of her students. But her lectures are long, boring, and tough to understand at times due to her strong accent. The midterm was randomly thrown onto us two days before the due date, in which the wrong time was told. Subpar lectures and unclear instructions define this.

(I had Qing for 201, not 202, but it wasn't an option) 

Professor Qing is an exceptional, extremely caring professor. If you want to 4.0 the class, go to her office hours and do her honors option! She gives extra credit (unlike other JMC professors) and show your appreciation for her. Nevertheless, try your best and your work will be recognized.

Professor Qing is one of the sweetest and most understanding professors I have ever had, and she is very knowledgable on a variety of political science and IR topics. Her class is somewhat disorganized and instructions for essays and assignments can be somewhat unclear, but she is usually more than willing to answer any questions you have.

I appreciated that Professor Qing took the time to make sure we understood her lectures (she recognises that her accent is hard to understand). My biggest problem is that her guidelines for assignments are incredibly vague.

I love Dr. Qing! I really enjoyed her MC 201 course. She was very accessible outside of class and got to know us as people in addition to students. Her research is very interesting. She was a fair grader and attending office hours was really helpful. She is very sweet and I'm so glad to have developed a relationship with her. 100% recommend!

analysis.name: Rebecca Sullivan
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: One of the best professors here at MSU. Engaging and relevant lectures, clear homework instructions, and cares about students. Make sure you attend lectures.

Amazing professor, gives tons of extra credit and no one grade is going to massively hurt you. Her online lectures are actually well-thought out, the slides are genuinely helpful, and the quizzes directly pull from them. She also actively takes feedback on what activities actually help teach the content, take this class with her if you can!

I am glad to have taken this course, with one of the best professors at Michigan State. Professor Sullivan truly cares about how her students learn from her course setup and asks for input on how to improve and help students receive the most from the course.  I can't recommend her enough. if you can take her course jump on it you won't regret it!
Easy class to 4.0. No exams just group work but she's an easy grader. Overall great professor!

Professor Sullivan is a great teacher for Marketing 300. She allows the class to be structured how the students want (fully in-person, hybrid, fully online, etc.) and allows us as the student body to choose what we want out of this course. She gives a weekly quiz and discussion posts, but you'll be set as long as you go to class and listen.

analysis.name: Rabindra Ratan
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Writing this review in advance lol. But Robby is honestly great and makes the class not even feel like it's an upper level 400 class. If you still need to take MI 401 then I highly suggest that you choose this professor. There is attendance every week so just make sure you're logging on/coming to class. Class content is really engaging and in VR

My only problem with this class was the use of AI. He doesn't have lecture notes for the topics he assigns, instead you have to interact with an AI chatbot (Gemini or GPT). Other than that, hes great, the class is hardly difficult and it can be fun at times.
One of my favorite professors at msu, i took his avatar and vr class because of how easy his class is. The only way to fail is literally if you don't do your work

Robby seems like a good guy and the class isn't very difficult but that doesn't give him an automatic 5/5. 4.0 is 94-100. He is super disorganized. Everything in D2L is a link to a google doc. Not sure why he can't just post to D2L like every other professor. Grading expectations were confusing. Responded to emails quick but feedback wasn't helpful

Robby is a great professor who is very passionate about virtual reality and avatars. He encourages a positive, accepting, and inclusive environment. I can't forget to mention how absolutely fun the class is. Having group discussion/activities in VR is SERIOUSLY fun. A class where you learn while flying around on a magic cushion is unforgettable.

analysis.name: Rajeev  Yadav
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This prof isn't even involved in the course. TA's run it, they're unhelpful and rude. This class is more handwriting than chem. Projects are straightforward but little direction is given. >2 hours per session is just writing redundant details. It's run like a high school chem class. Easy to 4.0. All this extra work for no good reason.

My software glitched and so instead of a complete PDF, only the final page was actually submitted on a team project. After realising the mistake, the professor wouldn't accept the fixed version, saying that it is an insignificant part of the grade, and that it didn't matter. the assignment was worth 15% of the grade...

For 1 credit, this class gives a hell of a workload. All work is due within 48 hours (or less) of your lab time, so it feels very condensed. How easy this class is also depends a lot on your lab group.  Rubrics are available for each assignment type, pay attention to them. The course gets a bit easier once you get the hang of each assignment type.

The lab was super fun but it all depends on your group. If you have a bad group then you will do bad in the lab. The ULAs are hit or miss but mine were great and clear. The projects were interesting just a lot of lab reports and writing.

Really difficult to ask questions and get actual answers. Had to contact the ULA to get actual feedback. Would tell you to do one thing and then come back later and ask why you had you lab set up that way. Made no sense.

analysis.name: Stephen Rachman
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 26 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Rachman's main focus is that you know how smart he is; nothing else matters. He can be funny and engaging, and he loves to drop in pop culture references every change he gets, but if you have a funnier narrative, what you get is a teenage boy who wants to forever impress his mommy!
Lectures are long and boring. This class is a class that most people take for an IAH requirement so it feels too strict and high stakes to actually learn.

If I could say one thing about him, it would be that he needs to acknowledge that his prerequisite classes are not that interesting to most people that are required to take them. He was also a little unorganized when it came to due dates and it's obvious he likes to hear himself talk. Overall the class was easy, but had lengthy and boring content.

Rachman was great, you can tell he loves his job. He got to know students and would often remember things we wrote or talked about. He gives informative yet fun feedback and is quite forgiving in terms of grading. It's a reading heavy class, a new text or parts of a book every week, there are some good films in there too. All around a good class.

I took professor Rachman's 221C course and loved every minute of it. Fair warning: there is a lot of assigned reading, most of which are stories and not textbook reading. In this course we were mainly graded on papers and attendance. If you show up and write the papers well you'll have nothing to worry about.

analysis.name: Saroopa  Taylor
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 64 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: She is so nice. I have a 98% in this class its very easy. Just do the work and you're good. She offers extra credit and grades work super fast. I emailed her about an issue and she responded within minutes and fixed the issue. I love her, she's so sweet I'd do anything for her. Please take this class and show her love.

She is such a sweet teacher; you can tell she loves her job and teaching this subject. I really like her classes and hearing her talk. She takes your answers from the homework and incorporates them into the next lecture. She's very open to feedback and will adjust her class and teaching format to keep her students happy. I enjoy her class.

Literally one of the kindest professors I've ever had. Always receiving and listening to feedback, knows all her students and you can tell she loves her job. Weekly homework but it's never difficult and no exam, just a group presentation.

Dr. Taylor is my pride and joy. Had her for 202 and 208L, amazing experience in both would take a million times over. So kind, helpful, understanding, funny, smart, everything you want in a professor. learn to use excel beforehand and the class is much easier. If you have the chance to take her, do it! Praise Dr. Taylor, she deserves the world.

Her lectures are really fun and easy to relate with in real life scenarios and she also addresses present day issues. Grading isn't too strict but will give useful comments to improve on, a lot of group work. If she sees potential, she helps give resources and references how to succeed and do more outside of class. Took the class for fun, worth it!

analysis.name: Ted Richards
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 29 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I found this course difficult due to its grading structure and heavy workload. The syllabus categories made it hard to track my standing, and missing grades in a section impacted my GPA. I reached out for help over 2.5 weeks but didn't get the guidance I needed. Stay proactive and clarify expectations early.

One of the hardest class I have had. He is nice, but the class is not easy at all. DONT SKIP CLASS. 4 exams in total, 3 outside of class, Final is cumulative and in person. Assignments twice per week (pick 3 questions from exercise you want to talk about in class, and what are some questions you want to ask him). Ask him if you have any question.

Dr. Richards is an amazing and entertaining lecturer.  I would say the grading was a bit unfair. It is tier-based, so if you understand the class and consistently earn perfect grades on all homework and essays, you can still receive a poor grade for attendance, reading questions, or something else.  Please do not take if not interested in soccer.

The content is not the easiest to understand but he does a great job at making it digestible and tailors his lectures to the students that are attending class so he can really help you with the things you struggle with. Very high energy and does a great job at keeping people engaged.

Really easy class. Lectures can get kind of boring but when attendance is done at the beginning you can leave early. Reading question homework assignments a few times a week that are super easy and one paper like once every other friday thats only 600 words. You can tell Dr. Richards enjoys his job and a 4.0 is attainable with some work.

analysis.name: Todd Surline
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Todd is the best professor I have ever had. He truly cares about each and every student. He gives quizzes and exams that are exclusively based off of lecture/book and are extremely fair. There is one group project but he broke it into steps to help you. I would recommend this class to everyone no matter their major!

Todd is the sweetest and most caring professor at Michigan State. He's passionate about teaching and wants his students to succeed. Exams and quizzes are very fair all based on the lectures, and there's one group project with plenty of time to complete and provides in class time. Attendance isn't mandatory, but it's definitely worth going!

Todd is the sweetest man ever. He cares so much about his students and it is clear he wants us all to succeed. He is the owner of an HR consulting firm, and his expertise shows through his lectures. I cannot say enough good things about him really, would recommend taking this course.

Really great class to take, very informative to learn about. Professor Surline is a great professor, very understanding and knows what he is teaching about. He is such a sweet guy and cares about his students. Was really accommodating when going through a family death. Pay attention and you will get a good grade. Def recommend taking this course.

Todd is a great and easy professor! He's really understanding of any situations and has a lot of experience in the professional field that translates well in class. Would def recommend, he's a sweet guy for sure.

analysis.name: Thomas Rimer
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 87 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Took FI320 for my business minor. He explains concepts in an easy way to understand and gives lots of examples. The tentative schedule is easy to follow and helpful. Practice problems are optional, but help a lot with assignments. If you read and watch lectures, you're gonna learn the concepts. Would recommend taking this before an ACC class.

He bases your entire grade on 3 exams and 5 assignments. He also forces everyone to buy an expensive textbook that you barely use because he creates videos for every small piece of information, in which the slides he uses are not available due to "people just using the slides instead of watching the lectures." Take any other professor if possible

I liked this class. Learned a lot as someone who is not a finance person. The class is lecture heavy but if you follow the tentative schedule he has you'll be fine. I found a lot of overlap between lectures videos and textbooks so I usually just watched the videos and downloaded the textbook chapters in case I needed info from there on the exam.

Their laughter dances like sunlight through pages, turning every moment into warmth.
Together, they write a story of love that even time leans in to read.

analysis.name: David Baylis
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 32 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He is a really good guy and I really enjoyed his class, just not what I expected based off the syllabus. Lots of group work but it isn't anything hard, just takes some time. No final, year long group project combined with other classes but he makes stuff do in steps so it wasn't bas at all. Lots of outside work like interviewing and visiting cites.

The workload is fairly balanced, and you don't really have to watch all of the movies he requires as long as you know some of the story. He's a pretty chill guy with fair grading and an easy class even if you don't like writing that much although the projects are a little annoying to do.

Very caring and nice guy. Understands that many are taking to fulfill requirements, and I feel is accommodating to those students whilst challenging students who want to dive deeper. Very fair with grading, and tests are clear-cut as long as you take notes. Find a good group at the beginning and you're set. I learned quite a bit from his class.

Baylis is such a funny guy. His assignments seem like a lot but actually don't take that much time. He always provides great feedback and is very accessible outside of class. Participation really matters! His exams are on the harder side if you don't know what was discussed in lectures and in class readings. Overall awesome professor!

I don't usually leave reviews about classes, but this teacher went above and beyond, he genuinely wants you to learn and do well in this class. Most of the work done is in group projects based off the lecture materials. He often holds optional classes where you can come for extra support on projects or just to ask questions.

analysis.name: Elizabeth Connors
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I've never had a professor actively sabotage/undermine my academic and professional life until now. I won't get into specifics for fear of her seeing this but she was not only working against me the whole semester, she implied herself into my professional life unknown to me. Taking her class was not only a bad thing for school but also for my life

Grades very strictly and does not provide individual feedback on quizzes, which makes it hard to learn from mistakes. The material itself is manageable, but the grading focuses heavily on small details, so even minor errors can significantly lower your score. Be prepared to rely on your own understanding and outside resources to improve.

By far the worst accounting professor at MSU, if you even consider her class accounting related. She wouldn't criticize your work, she would criticize you. Her big rule was to not ask any questions in class. The effect she has on her students life is extremely negative, and the material she teaches has zero application to anything.

She has a really bad attitude when it comes to teaching and is pretty rude to students. The class was not terrible but her participation structure is really annoying and forces you to ask questions on the discussion board and you have to compete with the person asking the most questions. Connors is always complaining and talking down to students.

Professor Connors makes it tough for you to want to show up to class and frankly do anything for her class. She is a tough grader and gives little to no leeway when it comes to attendance. She expects you to show up to every single class and ask questions throughout the semester despite her class being hard to follow and extremely boring.

analysis.name: Mark Becker
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I took PSY 302 with Dr. Becker and loved it. The lectures are all super interesting, he's a very funny guy, and attendance is optional. The exams can be kinda tough, but he'll curve them if everyone isn't doing well. Grades are based off of 3 exams and several interesting labs graded for completion. If I could take another class with him, I would.

Dr. Becker is a great professor who made class interesting. He does mostly lectures from slides, but the content is interesting and he elaborates. Tests are tough and although attendance isn't mandatory, most of the information can't just be found on the slides. He made the online labs we did and I really enjoyed doing them.

Very smart professor who teaches in a way that is easy to understand. Exams are challenging, but if you go to lecture and study ahead of time you will be fine. Labs are really easy and also a great way to help you understand what we are learning in class. He also has a sense of humor which makes the class a bit less intimidating.

I like how he explains concepts during lecture. I type what he says & it sticks to my brain. Exams are a little challenging, but he gives a review that helps a lot. You're required to do some SONA studies online that are mostly easy (surveys or in person tasks of your choice). There's a lot of online lab experiments, but they're easy points, EC yes

Good professor who understands that students have unexpected situations that may affect grades or exam times. Mostly read off lecture powerpoints but gave good explanations to every concept and clearly knew what he was talking about. A bit intimidating.

analysis.name: Douglas Bessette
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Don't worry about the time slot for the lecture, it's only for half a semester (ends when spring break starts). Bessette actually cares about you and is so funny to listen to. The chillest professor ever.

Dr. Douglas Bessette has been an excellent instructor who brings a wealth of knowledge and passion to his classes, especially in the field of clean energy and sustainability. His teaching style is both engaging and approachable, creating a comfortable learning environment where students are encouraged to participate and share their insights.

Dr Bessette is the best professor I have ever taken a class with here at MSU. Dr Bessette has a clear passion for what he teaches and he really does not care about your grades, only that you engage with the material and try. His lectures are fun and I enjoyed going to his class each week. Plus, he gives you a cheat sheet for the exams.

He was such a great prof! Material was relatively easy to get through, the assignments were easy as well. Wasn't too harsh of a grader as long as you did the assignments correctly. I really enjoyed the topic of this class, partially because Professor Bessette made it interesting, and I know other students in the course feel the same.
Hilarious, knowledgeable, approachable, entertaining.

analysis.name: Diana Bello-DeOcampo
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Took histology last semester and was by far one of the most interesting classes ive taken at MSU. However, this class was the most amount of work for a 4 credit class that I have taken at MSU. Lectures are short and this class requires a lot of outside reading in order to do well. She's a great prof but you need to do you own work to succeed.

IBIO 425 is a LOT of studying and information, but Dr. Bello is one of the most accommodating, kind, caring, and flexible profs at msu. If you ever need help, she'll meet with you one on one with zero judgement. Don't be afraid to talk to her, to ask silly questions, or even to give feedback. She listens to her students and acts on it.

Dr Bello was great, took her IAH 204 class in Spring, she has very lenient grading criteria and is very clear about the content on each exam. I didnt like biology at all, but she made the course very manageable plus she is fun to talk to before and after class. Attendence is important though since the class is lecture based. Easy course for ISB req

analysis.name: Bill Cooke
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Cooke is very kind and knowledgeable overall, but beware of the grading structure. The only grades that go in are 5-question quizzes and lengthy exams, so one wrong is an automatic 80%. Seemed manageable at first, but often the questions are worded very specifically to details that might've been glazed over or missed in lectures.
This is a great class and Professor Cooke is super knowledgeable.
Very nice Professor! All slides were posted to D2L, which was really nice. Tests and mini quiz questions were a little more difficult, but were manageable.

analysis.name: Jeff Biddle
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently

Not only was the class fun, but also interesting, and Professor Biddle was able to guide the class to great insights. I hope to take another class of his in the future.

Jeff Biddle was probably my best professor Freshman year. Clear teaching and balances fun with learning perfectly. I took his University Seminar(Social Sciences: Economics) at the UNiversity of Notre Dame.
Despite my grade, I feel like Mr. Biddle was not at fault. His class was fun and we had great discussions.
Great professor and the class was very interesting. This was my favorite class.
Great and interesting class where everyone respects the professors times.

analysis.name: Subir Biswas

analysis.name: Ben Marley

Exams are tough and you are given no study guide which he justifies for his sake

This class is hard because it's graded by a only few things, most of which are test-based. You HAVE to read the material and show up to every class or else you may miss something that will be on a quiz or an in-class activity. You may want to make a friend if you plan on skipping, which is important anyway because the exams are done with a partner.

He also replaces the lowest grades with the highest ones. He offers some in-class extra credit, so it's important to attend lecture. Overall, an annoying but fairly easy 4.0.

This guy makes no sense. Spent all the lecture times waffling about stuff not related to the assignments, has you do a reading and then doesn't discuss the reading in class, but then the assignments are about the reading? Some people liked it but not me

analysis.name: Bilal Sevinc
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: He can come across as really bland and monotone and can seem boring but if you actually pay attention he is actually funny and cares about what he is teaching. I mean you could read the textbook but if you just take lecture notes and look over them you will be great. I did not read the book and I got 100 on every exam. Only graded on the 3 exams.

The examples and real-life experiences shared during the lectures made it easy to understand the topics. The professor responds to emails in a short time. Caring about students and respectful. I highly recommend him.

I do not have enough good things to say about professor Sevinc. I took his ISS 327 class in person. Attendance was not mandatory but you receive extra credit if you attend class. His class structure and syllabus was structured and very organized. He is a easy grader and gives great feedback. I do not have enough good things to say about him!

The professor was very nice, although he did only read from the slides every class. The course is based on three 100 point exams which seems scary, but I attended every class and never read the textbook and got 100 on each of them. As long as you take decent notes and are able to keep up with the quicker speed, you'll be fine.

Your overall class grade is based on just three exams which sounds scary but the class is really easy if you just read the book. He always lets us out at least 10 minutes early and adds videos to the lectures to make the class more enjoyable. Super sweet professor. If he does lecture fast, all the informations in the book or an outline he posts

analysis.name: Bill Punch

THE WORST TEACHER EVER IN THE HISTORY OF CS..THAT'S ALL I HAVE TO SAY

CSE 232 is a tough class, but Punch is good. His personification of the C++ compiler was pretty funny. Start projects early and study smart for the hard exams. Easy 3.0 if you work hard

His class wasn't that easy but that god I took it before Nahum became the professor, Punch might not be the best teacher but he doesn't randomly screw you over by adding in spurious requirements and providing no support to you on Piazza.

All I know is that is he had been at MSU for a bit longer a lot more people would've done CSE as a major.

analysis.name: Andrea Bierema
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 29 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: the easiest class I've ever taken. Material isn't boring, grading is clear and uploaded into d2L, accepted late work for most assignments. Not that you'll need it, bc every assignment is pretty simple. If you get anything less than a 4.0 in this class and don't have extenuating circumstances consider dropping out of college

Very easy class, and very chill prof, it's almost impossible not to get a 4.0 in this class. I enjoyed the content, and even though you don't HAVE to read the book essentially I found it interesting in general. Lots of online platforms but you get the hang of it. Def take this class for an easy gpa boost.

This is a very easy course. Before taking this class I read that there are too many platforms we are required to do work on like packback, d2L, textbook, dr. Tatiana, etc. I think this was easy to grasp and every two weeks is a module that follows the same criteria, just diff topics. I held an 100% basically through the entire course.

She is a great professor. Makes it clear what is due and when. Many resources are available for help. You do need to buy a book that is used for a discussion board. No exams, just a course semester project due at the end of the semester which isn't the hardest thing ever. Group work, but have same group whole semester. Overall I'd take again.

Very easy class overall. Work is easy and you're also with a group. The quizzes we had to do were super easy you can directly get the answers and get a 100. The project that we had to do was fun and easy to do. The only thing is that the packback was a bit annoying and the book is cringe.

analysis.name: Rick Blackwood
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The most insane class I have taken at MSU. Easy class, you watch a movie once a week and have a couple of one-pagers about the readings, but Prof. Blackwood is the highlight of the class. Not only are his lectures unhinged but he shares lots of stories from his past. While attendance is mandatory, you always want to show up to see what he says.

Rick is an amazing professor who really cares about what and how we learned. Yes, class was early, but you were watching amazing movies all the time. Don't miss class because you'll miss out on great lectures and analyses that Rick provides throughout class. Would take it again just to have Rick as a professor again.

Rick is the greatest college professor I ever had the pleasure of meeting. He is just an absolute wealth of knowledge- not just about the industry but about so many things. He's someone who you want to learn absolutely everything you can from. One of the greatest resources not just in the MSU film program, but at MSU as a whole.

Once a week during class, you will watch a film. The discussions and analysis of the films is very interesting, but you do need to go to class, because there are weekly essays, along with the fact that attendance is graded harshly the more you miss. The professor is very nice and interesting.

If you are looking for someone that will give you something meaningful for your time this is the man. Professor Blackwood, and those who work within his classes, really care about the material, and greatly encourage curiosity. While attendance is mandatory you're not wasting your time going. Read the material it seriously teaching good life lessons

analysis.name: Robyn Bluhm
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: PHL344 was one of the best classes i took at MSU thanks to Dr.Bluhm. She is passionate and caring but also very clear and firm on her grading criteria, bc she is also very clear and thorough on her lectures and explains difficult concepts easily. Her course has changed my perspective on medicine and i recommend her course for anyone in pre-health.

Super interesting intro course for bioethcis! Dr. Bluhm makes the online course super easy to understand. Lots of reading, writing, and group discussion, but that is expected for an online bioethics course. Really fair grading and is super easy to get in contact with! She also gives great feedback. She really cares about her students! Easy 4.0.
Seems paranoid around male students. Clearly writes her own reviews and has written her own Wikipedia page (lol).

She's very passionate and knowledgeable about bioethics and the class was very interesting. She creates a very good learning environment in the class that encourages discussion all sorts of issues, controversial or not. I definitely think that if you are doing anything involving bioethics you should take a class with her!

Dr. Bluhm was easily one of my favorite profs at msu. She knows a ton about bioethics and explains things very clearly with examples. Everything we discussed was so interesting. The tests are 7 essay questions but it is not hard to do well. There are a few extra credit points on the exams. This is a pretty easy 4.0.

analysis.name: Blaire Morseau
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I LOVE Professor Morseau! She's genuinely one of the sweetest people ever! We had a lot of in class activities which we worked with the people around us on, but they were fairly easy. She also drops the lowest two of those so if you miss class then you're good. A discussion lead, three quizzes, and the final exam as well.

Super nice and caring. Very laid back class. Class is graded on a few quizzes that are easy if you simply show up and pay attention,  4 in class assignments that are graded on completion (this is her form of attendance grade), a final exam and a discussion lead (not as scary as it sounds).

I loved Professor Moreseau. She truly cared about the content she was teaching and knew how to make it interesting. Discussion lead was super collaborative which made it less nerve wracking. 10/10 recommend this class!

LOVED PROFESSOR MORSEAU! Had her for AIIS201 and was funny, understanding, and I looked forward to going to the class every week. We had different readings each class, and then went over it and had lecture. Extremely fun and would take it again!

analysis.name: Stuart Blythe
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Extremely rigid and stressful. 4.0 cutoff raised to 94. Attendance policy was not clearly enforced until around week 4, then grades were suddenly penalized with no drops or real makeups. Missing one class can ruin your grade. Heavy workload for a 2xx course and little openness to questions. Strongly avoid.

Two projects and attendance counts towards your grade, so don't skip! On-campus, the class was a breeze, online though. He made us take weekly quizzes and do an entire project with peer reviewing still. He's very unsure of himself and he wasn't prepared at all. Barely heard from him, due dates were very frequent. Try to find a more organized prof.

WRA 210!!! Super easy grading. If you turn in the projects asked you will receive a 4.0. You have plenty of opportunities to submit late work and fix work in general to receive full credit. This class involves coding and learning the basics. Your final exam is the portfolio you create and it's super easy to receive a 100% on that!
Really nice professor, very understanding. Material was covered in a way that was easy to understand. Also allowed for Zoom attendance, so very accessible. Would absolutely recommend!
Two major projects and a final exam. Stuart is funny in that awkward nerdy way. He cares about your learning.

analysis.name: Christina Blaschke
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Thompson is very passionate about what she teaches. Attendance is mandatory but you get three freebies. Guest speakers come each week to expand on content. There's weekly reflection papers for completion points and 3 noncumulative, open note + open book online exams. Also easy honors option, just an extra reflection paper.

Tina is an amazing prof! Her class was not difficult at all, she's very understanding, down-to-earth, and isn't a harsh grader. I definitely recommend taking her classes, she makes course materials easy to understand and doesn't sugar coat anything.
Tina was absolutely amazing, and even convinced me to pursue SW as a career. I am applying to MSW programs simply because of her. I cannot recommend her classes enough, she really loves her job.
Very kind professor. Very passionate about Social Work. Exams online and reflections due each Sunday but not hard at all.

I loved this professor. The only complaint I have is that there is a lot of reading but you'll just have to face facts that you just have to skim a lot of things. She is a caring person, organized, fair grader, and very clear about her expectations.

analysis.name: Kelley Blanck
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Kelley absolutely changed the trajectory of my college journey. As a psychology major, I was interested in taking this class, and now I am a double major in social work because of it. She brings in guest speakers, and she herself has a significant amount of experience in the field. Quizzes are easy and every other week, and papers every other week!

The professor was very nice and the class was easy 6 reflections and 6 open note quizzes. The only thing that was hard was the quizzes included a lot of stuff that wasn't talked about in class and very niche things from the book. The questions were also worded weird.

loved professor Blanck, most students weren't very interactive, but she was. The class is easy and catered to the social work major. she uses guest speakers to teach about real world experiences working in differing social work types, very accommodating. assignments are very easy. only downside is passing with a 93% which is only a 3.5

She was very sweet! There was one guest speaker a week, and homework was split between short online quizzes and short written responses. A very easy course, but she did a lot to keep it interesting. I had no problem reaching her outside of class hours, and she was flexible about attendance, grades, due dates, etc.

analysis.name: Rebekah Blesing
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: ignorant to how difficult the materials she has us work with are or doesn't care but either way in this class we had to work using foreign techniques to us w/o practice and are critiqued and graded. Graded on many aspects that it's hard to keep straight what needs to be added and hardly gives any in class time to work. WAY too much for a100 class

I really enjoy Prof. Blesing's class. I overall enjoyed her helpful feedback and the class was very motivating for artistic expression, though sometimes you felt you needed to bend your work to fit some of her preferences. You can probably get through this class without purchasing the art kit, she supplies many of the needed tools and resources.

She was a really nice professor. I'm not a studio art major, so I was nervous about taking a sculpture class as a requirement for my major, but she was really helpful and provided good guidance throughout every assignment. The kit for the class was really expensive however, and we didn't use half of what was in it - buy materials as you go.

I enjoyed taking Rebekah's class. She seems passionate about presenting new projects. She gives excellent suggestions but has more or of a "figure it out as go" approach. I would love to take another one of her classes in the future :)

I had a great experience in Rebekahs class she is a wonderful professor. She pushes her students to dive deep and think critically about their projects. Almost every class period you will have an opportunity to work on projects/homework.

analysis.name: Shlagha Borha

She was a good person, but the amount of times she cancelled class last minute was wild. Because my class was an 8:00 am, there was over ten times where I would be in the classroom and we would get an email saying class was cancelled, a few times even after class had started. The class itself was very disorganized, mostly due to many cancellations.

If you're into creative work and open to learn new perspectives, take this class! She is fun, caring, and despite some of the students making this class difficult for her because of circumstances unrelated to the class, she is empathetic and a kind grader. I loved her!

She cancels all the time very last minute so don't take an 8 am class with her. Her class is very easy. She will make you read outload sometimes and work in groups or partners. All work is easy and there is never homework.

The professor is not all that bad. the class is easy and the writing assignments are not hard. For me, she did not come off as rude or have a bad attitude. She did however cancel class last minute a LOT or change it to Zoom that was extremely annoying. there is also a lot of reading in class and group discussions

analysis.name: Ryan Black
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Do not take this class and avoid this professor if you care about your mental health and GPA. Just take it somewhere else I would not recommend! 4 years of college and this is one of the weirdest experiences with an online class. Hopefully MSU does something about him.
The class is super interesting but be prepared to get a bad grade even if you do the work and pay attention. The exam questions are meant to be trick questions he is literally out to get you

analysis.name: Silvina Bongiovanni

I loved her class! She is very fun, engaging, and makes phonetics interesting. I would take any class that she taught.

analysis.name: Scott Borgeson

Scott just read lectures every class we had and introduced a final group presentation as our exam which was worth the entrie final grade as he gave almost no assignments. Do not take IAH 231 with Scott Borgeson. He's a nice guy and is definitely passionate about linguistics but this class was awful. analysis.name: Andaluna Borcila

The exams weren't horrible, and I managed to get an A after studying a TONNNN. You will cry over this class. Try to do homework early so you can get help
