However, she did offer a lot of extra credit on the final (added up to 20% to midterm exam grade). Her intentions are there but her lack of organization makes the class difficult.

I will NEVER take this class with her again. Try to take this class in the spring with a different professor if you can. Lectures were unorganized and I lost points on the homework for problems she helped with. Make sure to go to the TAs instead (they grade them). D2L course was also never updated with lecture material, so you have to go to class.

The professor is a great person, BUT she was extremely disorganized. You have to go to class and take notes since nothing is posted online. If you miss class, then you will most definitely be behind. The overall grade in the class is determined only by harshly graded weekly homework assignments and 2 exams. Take this class with another professor!

analysis.name: Rene Crespin
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: It isn't said anywhere, but you should definitely take EC420 before this class. So far it is very regression heavy. The slides are the worst part of the class. Poorly made, spelling and grammar errors everywhere. Midterm is coming up and it is so hard to study if you want to read the slides. To be fair, the subject is pretty interesting.

Class structure is well taught. Majority of the material is being able to read and interpret graphs, basic econometrics but not rigorous whatsoever. Professor is willing to meet if you are having issues, attendance is not worth much. Don't let the other reviews deter you this class is a much better option than other ec 400 classes.
Lectures are easy to understand, homework is pretty easy, takes attendance regularly.

Knows plenty about education economics but not how to teach. Would read off poorly made slides that he refused to even post on D2L which makes it incredibly hard to study. Had no clear learning goals or objectives for each unit so I didn't know what to learn. What is actually on exams or his in-class essay is a mystery and I often was blindsided.

analysis.name: Tobin Craig
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 40 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: The class is taught by different guest lectures which is made clear in the beginning of the course. I really found this class to be interesting and enjoyed it thoroughly. I found Craig's lectures to be really engaging and funny. I didn't ever talk to this guy 1 on 1 but he seemed great from a distance, The exams are very hard though so be aware.

Dr. Craig is very knowledgeable and his lectures were amazing. The class has different guest lecturers and topics each class, all of which were interesting. But, the exams were very difficult as you're given little to no grading criteria and the answers they're looking for are very specific. Grading is tougher than a 100-level course should be.

Craig was honestly one of my favorite professors this semester. He truly knows his craft and lectures well. If you choose his class ensure you go to his office hours for participation. There's a lot of reading in this class however, participation in class discussions is highly encouraged but not forced. He is a hard grader however.

Professor Craig is a very good professor. He is quite anti-technology, so beware of that, but many of the PTCD faculty are. He is overall a great teacher though and makes himself very available. Not an easy professor, but if you pay attention in class and do most of the readings, you'll do just fine.

If you're a PTCD major this doesn't apply to you, as I am sure he is a great PTCD professor. Taking MC201 with him as a freshman was absolutely horrid. Very harsh grader. If you are someone who is not interested in political theory, and you were planning on taking him for any other type of class, don't.

analysis.name: Karenanna Creps
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I actually took Karenanna for TE 432, Learning Through Movement, and she was incredible. One of the few Education profs that have taught me applicable, real-world lessons and examples. She was so sweet and so fun to talk to, also extremely accommodating. I highly suggest her for this class.

She is super nice and easy to reach out to. I would send her my assignments to look over and she would always respond very quickly with helpful feedback. She lets you redo any assignment with a low grade even if it's from the beginning of the year. She makes learning fun and creative. Totally recommend her for Learning Through Drama.
Love her! Recommend 10/10 for the Learning through Drama class!! Easy to talk to:)

analysis.name: Sean Crosson
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Crosson is the greatest thing to ever walk into a biology classroom. He is super nice and very eager to help students understand the material. The class is flipped, which takes some getting used to, but he always does a recap at the beginning of class, which is very helpful. Also he had a little texas accent so he is fun to listen to.

Dr. Crosson is probably the best BS 161 professor you can find at MSU, however, he only teaches every 2 years so be mindful when you are scheduling for this class. Every other BS 161 professor needed to be switched out in the middle of the semester except for him because he was actually knowledgable on the topic unlike the others as I hear it.

Dr. Crosson is a thorough professor and is good at what he does. He is very knowledgable in the content and is super caring/understanding! The book is required, but it does not really help that much and the main content is in the lectures/ICAS. Extra credit opportunities are offered for exams 1-3(1 point each). I recommend him!

BS 161 was a very difficult and consuming class, but Dr. Crosson and his TAs/UALs were phenomenal. Without them I would have failed this class without a doubt, but they did an amazing job of helping every student who needed it and explaining the why behind the processes. Dr. Crosson is truly a great professor, and I wish I could have him again.

Hard class, but great professor. You get used to the stupid schedule, but it's a flipped classroom, so you teach yourself everything, then recap with questions and examples in class. Lot's of homework and studying. Iclicker questions also count for a grade. Crosson is great at answering questions in depth, so try and you'll be fine.

analysis.name: Robert Cummiskey
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Love this guy. I had a mental health crisis halfway through the semester and went from being there everyday to missing most classes. He was super understanding and had no problem accommodating me through that time. Also a super light grader as long as you put effort in. I would happily take this course again if I had to, great GPA boost.

I loved Dr. Bob! He made a gen-ed writing class very enjoyable. There are only 5 essays, or "projects" that you have to complete over the course of the semester, and as long as you stick to the rubric you will be fine. On top of being hilarious, he also gave me really good feedback that I could put towards my future essays.

Bob is a great and funny guy. The class he teaches is pretty easy. As long as you show effort, you'll get a good grade. The only problem is that he talks a lot. His lectures can go on a very long time because he goes on long tangents and repeats himself often. Other than that he's very helpful and nice. His lectures can drag but he's still great.

If you want a professor who genuinely cares about you, Mr. Cummiskey is your guy. He is super considerate and is willing to work with you if you communicate. Great teacher, would definitely recommend for WRA 101.

Prof. Cummiskey is very casual and a great guy to interact with. If you show up to class and participate, he'll remember you and be more likely to help out when you need it. Class was very easy, mostly documentaries with writing projects throughout the semester. Very easy class to take for the IAH credit, plus it's a very fascinating subject.

analysis.name: William Crank
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 30 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I appreciate that he used his own experiences in the business in lectures, as that gave applications and context to lectures. However, that's how he gave lectures. Almost purely through his own experiences. You have so few opportunities to earn a grade, so every little thing matters. This course caused so much stress. If you can, avoid his classes.

Yea so William Crank got cranky and made me stay after class to give me a lecture on being on time. I also was surprised by how much he bragged. He would  brag about things way off topic all time. If you tell him you know something he might argue you or brag he is better at it.

Honestly, he was not a bad professor. He does really care about the future of his students and constantly would bring up opportunities and opened himself up to help guide students which I thought was really nice. The exams are a little hard but if you show up to class you will understand whats going on. The group project was pretty easy too.

I am currently taking PR 305 with him this class is easily the worst class I have taken at msu He does not make any assignment clear every assignment he will not provide exact details of what he wants us to include. Most of the time he just talks about himself & prides himself that his exams r 15 pages single spaced & that they are not passable.

Crank is a piece of work. Easily one of the worst professors on campus, but is a God in his own mind. Never take this man, as he will make your semester 10x harder than it needs to be. (He is also the type of guy to read all these negative views on him, and conclude everyone but him is the problem.)

analysis.name: Curtis VanDonkelaar
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Curtis is an entertaining professor who cares a lot about his students, loves his job, and grades easily. That being said, he also assigns a myriad of homework at times, but he is very flexible with due dates. His lectures often have groupwork, and many assignments are peer review, so beware if that is not up your alley.

He is a really nice guy and if you participate a little he is super willing to help you and be accommodating. He does not put grades in which sucks but he gives you a lot of time for each project and gives really good feedback. Just show up and do the work and you'll be fine. He says attendance is mandatory but you can miss 2-3 times.

Doesn't put in grades until last minute BUT it's a fair and good amount of workload, if you miss one class you're fine. You get 4 absences through the semester. He's very very very caring and understanding and wants you to learn and understand course material. He is an amazing professor and very passionate of what he teaches.

He was an amazing professor, but my only complaint is that he did not grade any assignments until after finals, so I worried a bit about how he grades. All the assignments are very clear to complete and he allows you to turn in assignments late. Not a harsh grader, got a 4.0 in the class.

Really nice and caring guy. He just wants you to show up and participate. Do the work and you'll get a 4.0. Overall super easy class with an even better professor. Highly recommend taking this course with him.

analysis.name: Katharine  Currie
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Currie made an easy class way too difficult. She explains things well but doesn't set you up for success. Her lectures miss a lot of important info and her exams are almost impossible to take. Her lab assignments also seem so useless and set you up for a low grade. If she wants students to do better she should redesign her slides and assignments.

She never adds any of the important points during lecture into her slides. If you want to succeed in this class, you have to heavily take notes which is almost impossible. Her exams are so bad and impossible to study for. She also does not set up assignments very well. If you miss one thing, you are not allowed to complete other requirements.

Professor Currie's lectures are long and have a lot of confusing info, I found it easier to not attend and study it at my own pace. However, she gives few extra credit points for attendance. The labs were frustrating for me as the pre quizzes were hard and you dont get alot of time. The lab TAs dont really help you for the lab reports either.

The material is interesting. The class would be so much better with a different professor though. Great person. Not great at explaining things. Some student have done really well. I am not one of those students. The material is confusing and she confuses me more with the way she explains things. Overall, this class sucks but you can do well in it.

analysis.name: Everardo Cuevas
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He claimed that my paper was done by ai, which it wasn't and gave me a horrible grade. There was nothing I could do cause it was the end of the year. He is ALWAYS late to class and will cancel it 10 min before it starts when everyone is already in the classroom. Unprofessional and expects a lot when he doesn't hold himself to the same standards.

Dr. Eve was an amazing professor that taught a very well structured English class. He was very caring to all students and grades pretty leniently. Do your work when assigned and you should be able to easily get a 4.0.

Professor Cuevas is an excellent teacher. He's fun, helpful, and genuinely passionate about teaching — something that's increasingly rare these days. A professor who actively engages with students and truly wants them to learn already goes above and beyond. Show up to class, put effort into your projects/peer reviews and you'll 4.0 this course.

Professor Cuevas is truly one of the best professors I have had at MSU. He is so laid back and understanding. Communication is key in his class and despite any sense of intimidation you may have, there is no way to fail unless you are simply not even trying. Always always communicate with Cuevas and your results in this course will be great!

I really recommend Eve, he is a great guy along with an amazing teacher. Attendance is required for this class by the school, and the class is graded based on 5 projects/attendance. You should get a 4.0 if you show up and put in effort into the projects/online posts. The only thing that sucks is the grading scale used by the school - 94% is a 3.5

analysis.name: Oscar Cuncic
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: He is the co-lecturer with prof Bauer. He teaches stuff really well in lectures. He will explain questions with great detail and I really enjoy attending his class. Sometimes he will even put corresponding hw questions on presentation slides. Turns out I believe this is a better way of teaching since we now truly understand how this question works.

His lectures were interesting and easy to follow. You can tell he enjoys teaching. Attendance is required and he uses iclicker to check the grades. The test study guides he makes are important. If you can do those, you can do the exam.  He has a generous extra credit policy.

Professor Cuncic is very passionate about physics. He is helpful and responsive to feedback. He is exactly what I would hope for from a physics professor at MSU. I am happy with how things turned out in this course and I would take any course with him teaching.
Attendance is mandatory. His lectures covered what would be on the exams, also the practice exams were similar to the exams. But the class is almost entirely based on exam grades.
Very passionate in his lectures. Participation matters a fair amount regarding iClicker. Practice exams are extremely similar to the real exams.

analysis.name: Allison Cupples
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This class is not hard but you do need to make sure you go through the lectures and review before exams because the exams are not open note. Her lectures are kind of boring but make sure to pay attention bc it will be on the exams and homework. The final exam is not cumulative it just a regular exam.

Overall, a great class and professor. Everything you need to know she teaches you in lecture, the book is a nice addition but not necessary. The exams are a little challenging and require knowledge from lectures and homework, but overall, pretty fair. Attendance/participation not really required as she has recorded lectures on D2L. HWK once a week.

On exams be prepared to be tested on calculations as well as definitions and fill in the blank. If you go to lectures you should have no problem in this class. Cuppules is an amazing professor who prepares you for hw and exams extremely well with class lectures, I would recommend making flashcards for definitions, take notes

Nice lady! The notes she gives are clear and the homework is totally manageable and actually helps with the exams. The lectures could stand to be a little more interesting, but overall a good class, and an easy A.

analysis.name: Cynthia Goff
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She is a really good professor! The homework is actually helpful and never took me more than 20 or 30 minutes. She does expect participation from everyone, but makes it super easy to contribute. Sometimes the lectures can feel a little repetitive, but overall I loved her class!
Loved Cynthia! I'm taking her again next semester and looking forward to it!
she is amazing and personable. she is very understanding about everything and willing to be flexible if needed.

She was an amazing teacher. She is also very big on working with people in groups. So, if you do take her class work with people you enjoy talking to and participate. Otherwise, the class is going to go slow, and you will not want to go to class. Get the textbook, you don't really need it for homework, but you will need it for papers.

She is my favorite professor I have ever had. Gives you a chance to correct mistakes that you may have made on your quizzes. She is there to help you at all times and is super understanding if you need an extension on a project. Absolutely amazing. Highly recommend taking a class with her if you can!!!!!

analysis.name: Alison Cupples
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Cupples is fantastic. All information on exams and homework is gone over in class. Lectures can be a little boring, but overall she is a good professor and prepares you well for exams. As long as you go to class this is an easy A.

One of the best professors I've had. She is extremely kind and her lectures are great. The homework follows the lecture examples and the tests are very similar to the homework. If you show up and pay attention, you'll be fine.

WORST PROFESSOR EVER!!!! I missed class once, and you're allowed to miss three, and i will be lucky to 1.5 this class. It's so hard, she is TERRIBLE and extremely unhelpful. She expects you to memorize all the material and then decides to not test you on the "performance objectives" that she tells you to know. Avoid her at all costs!!!!

analysis.name: Cynthia Craig
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Went to FLorence on study abroad with her. EXCELLENT teacher and travel companion!
wow, she is such a powerful force of nature...the best prof i have had yet!!!!!!

analysis.name: Cynthia Gabriel
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: There's too much for just 350 characters, but I will say be prepared for your final to be a big group project. She is very unclear with what she wants, didn't know how to use D2L so I had no idea where I stood in the class. Her class was interesting in the beginning but quickly becomes extremely dull. I'd say the only plus is there was only 1 exam.

I love the way this class was organized.  We didn't just read from one text book.  It was interesting.  We read from several books (usually only 2-10 pages a time for hw), watched several short YouTube clips and if you attend class each day (very little participation required) you can easily understand and pass this class. Super interesting!

She is extremely confusing. Everything is thrown onto the syllabus including due dates (which are changed verbally but not on the syllabus) so any time there is an assignment you have to dig through the entire syllabus. For a university requirement class the workload is a lot (if you actually do everything).  Conclusion: unorganized

unlike the other rater i loved our project because she gave us time in class to work on it. it was actually quite easy. and interesting. she gave us a lot of creative freedom with the project. and i thought the discussions were really interesting, but i didn't love listening to the rest of the students so much.

For a class with more than 200 people I can't believe how "small" she makes this class feel. I got to know other students. I love her lecture style. Some students want more "textbook"-style, but I prefer the way she has an organization structure to lecture but just talks without notes.

analysis.name: Maxine Davis
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 45 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Course is a lab so it will be ran by ULAs. Be hopeful that you have amazing ULAs that you can ask for help with. Dr. Davis would have multiple sections at once & rarely appeared in my section. When she did appear, she asked questions but would make it more confusing. She is such a nice and kind professor although her teaching is another story.

She was great. She was there to help whenever and was easy to acess during office hours and email! The ULA's do a lot but she is always there making sure they are correct and help out whenever needed. My only complaint is the grades came in very late and sudden at the end of the semester.

She was nice and helpful when needed, but overall a poor teacher and grader. Instructions for lab write-ups were inconsistent and scattered, making them hard to follow. She graded everything at the end, so I didn't know I was doing things wrong and got low scores. Group work grading was unfair since everyone shared the same grade.

Your experience will vary greatly depending on your ULA's and lab partners, but Dr. Davis herself was accessible inside and outside of class which was helpful. Assignments are fairly easy as long as you follow the rubric exactly and communicate with ULA about the exact expectations and what they specifically want to see.

Professor Davis is one of the best lab professors I have had at MSU. She's okay at explaining things and may take a moment to articulate her thoughts but she makes sure you understand what's happening and is willing to help at any point during the lab. Overall, I would highly recommend her to anyone taking this class!

analysis.name: Cy Stewart
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 52 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: The required textbook was edited by him and has several typos.  His lectures are loud and obnoxious. He's rude. The tests are all true/false, watch out for the wording.  While attendance is optional, he adds a lot of stuff in the lectures that you can't get from the book.  My advice, do not take a class with this prof.

He seems like a very nice guy, but he repeats all of his stories a million times. Plus, his stories never seem to relate to the topic. They are so long that by the time he is done, I cant remember what he was talking about. However I do have to say that the class is really not hard. If you read the book and come to class, you should have no problem

To everyone claiming that Cy is "soo hard" ...welcome to college. You cannot expect your professors to spoon-feed you answers to future exams in lectures, or be able to find those answers verbatim in your texts. Cy gives you the proper tools to make the larger inferences yourself. If you can't succeed at this, it's not him, it's YOU.

Good gosh. I have never had such an easy class. The tests are all true/false!! Honestly! How can you fail?? He gives you a take-home final for god's sake! If you don't understand him, I suggest expanding your vocab. He *does* use some higher level language, but no more than is expected of college students. Too bad he's retiring soon.

he repeats himself like 50 times, he is obsessed with stating tremendously large exaggerative vocab words, it would be understandable if he talked like that on the regular, but i guess if you feel because you are an prof, you have to be extraordinarily hard on purpose, but not all profs can do that.  Its a fine line between not being cont...

analysis.name: Sejuti Das Gupta
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I really enjoyed Professor Das Gupta; she makes sure you understand the content and even gives visual aids. Her midterm was open-note, and she even let us redo our first essay after she graded it and left comments. Her lectures are filled with examples that help us understand the content; just be ready to participate, but her office hours help!

Professor was amazing! I was out for a month due to illness, and she was extremely accommodating and helpful with me and had great feedback. There's a lot of reading and work, but it's worth it and I definitely feel like I learned a lot.

201 is all lecture based, and Das Gupta did an amazing job. Her lectures were fascinating and very informative. All exams and papers were easy and fit the content. Das Gupta put together an amazing team of lecturers, and the topics were diverse. From the U.S. to India, from Brazil to Syria, Das Gupta covered interesting stuff and did a great job.

Das Gupta is the best teacher I have ever had here at MSU so far, and will probably sustain that role for the years coming. She is not only good at teaching and making sure we understand what is happening in class, she cares about her students and their well-being. Would 1000% recommend taking any class you can with her.

When subbed in for Prof. Elmo, my grade went from bad to good. She was so accessible outside of class and willing to help. When asking for feedback, she went through my paper step by step with me over what she thought I could improve on, it was amazingly helpful when it came down to polishing the draft of my essay. Overall, super caring and helpful

analysis.name: Don DeVeaux
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor DeVeaux has been one of the best professors I have ever had during my time at MSU. He cares so deeply for his students by structuring his course in a way that is both digestible and challenging. His lectures are so well prepared and very interesting. It truly reinforced my passion for Marketing and Market Research as a career.

Professor DeVeaux prepares you for the future. There are a good amount of homework and reading assignments, but they are all relevant to the following lectures. The course is very structured on D2L in order to reduce stress and confusion when navigating the course website. He is an incredible lecturer and an even better person. Enjoy his courses.

Professor DeVeaux is a good professor. At times it didn't feel like we had a clear rubric to follow specifically for the Group project. But he was an overall good professor offers support when you need it
Great professor, wants you to succeed and give you the materials to help you.

Professor DeVeaux is one of the only professors I have had at MSU who genuinely cares about his students and their professional futures. Despite his Master's curriculum being noted as rather "hard" (esp projects course) if you are someone who is willing to put in the time and communicate mistakes openly... you'll be just fine! And prepared for job

analysis.name: Justin Detmers
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Detmers was by far my favorite professor from my time at MSU. He made me realize how much easier it is to learn and understand when classes/lectures are engaging. His lectures are fun and engaging while still being content rich.He cares about his students and their learning as well as improving the way he teaches.

I had Professor Detmers during senior year and 5th yr teaching internship. He is a fantastic person, both in and out of class. He genuinely cares you and is very accessible. He makes lessons fun and engaging, filled with comedy as well as meaningful moments. I highly recommend connecting with Dr. Detmers as a mentor during your studies. Go Green!
I loved Justin!! He gets to know every one of his students and teaches things that are actually helpful in the classroom. He is really funny and makes the 3 hour lectures go by fast.

Really nice guy! You can tell he's educated on the topics of this class and actually cares to take the time to get to know his students/ care about their well being. Lectures are engaging for the most part- There isn't an excessive amount of homework. Only one or two assignments a week but the reading does take a bit of time.
He's hilarious, caring, smart and just one of the greatest professors I have had

analysis.name: Denise Troutman
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 37 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: A perfect example of why the tenure system should be discontinued. She does not do her job well, and makes herself unclear with her projects. She is the worst professor you will ever have, so make sure to get out of her class while you still can.

She was very unhelpful. Her syllabus tells you one thing, but then she'll tell you something completely different. Her grading was very difficult and there was absolutely no way to please her. If you did not share the same ideas as her or talk a bunch, you might as well just accept the 2.0 in her class because there's no chance of anything better.

What an awful teacher. Do not take her class. In order to get a 4.0, you have to get a 96% and she will do anything she can to find a reason to give you a poor grade. On top of this, she is also a narcissist. One of our assignments was to interview her! Please do not take her class. You will regret it if you do.

It took almost a month for her to get stuff graded, which made me drop the class, since I wasn't risking bad grades. The course layout was confusing and disorganized because everything was just dumped into three tabs. The schedule was also dumped into one spot. It is so much nicer when only one module is available at a time!

She is the harshest grader I have experienced, I would never take this class again or have her as a teacher. Class is way too long and you have to have your camera on if you want to get participation, hate this class and would not suggest.

analysis.name: Philip Delekta
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 46 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: The first day of class the other professor who ran the course, along with the ULAs and TA, told us that Phillip Delekta makes it borderline impossible to get a 4.0 in the class. The content itself if easy, but he makes it difficult to get anything above a 3.5 on the exams. Very strict professor, so don't expect any leniency. Class average is 3.0.

This class is designed for you to suffer. I am a 4.0 student so I know how to study. One MCQ is worth 4 points and you can only lose 48 points in the class to not 4.0. No wiggle room. His TAs somehow find a way to take at least 2 points off of every worksheet on top. The whole teaching team is a cult wanting you to suffer. Please avoid this guy.

The homework is easy and quick and the exams repeat homework questions so they're not bad either. It's an annoying class but it's not difficult.

You have to go to his lectures every Friday. They're super boring but you can just do other work during the class because the lectures don't really have anything to do with the homework/exams. Homework was super easy, exams weren't bad and have same questions as the homework. It's an annoying class but not hard.

analysis.name: Brandy Ellison
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 44 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor has a superiority complex and was very condescending to me and other students whenever we needed help. Her instructions are never clear when assignments are due when it comes to weekly assignments or the big projects. The material itself is not difficult; however, the professor is difficult to deal with.

Professor Ellison was difficult to gauge, she was nice on occasion but there were times where a group member would go up to ask for clarification on an assignment and she was condescending in her response. Easy class if you do your work, you can easily get an A, but I found lectures disengaging even when I actually was interested in the material.

Overall, this class is manageable. The weekly quizzes and assignments were due at the same time every week, so remember deadlines; she does not give late credit. You work in groups pretty much all semester and have 2 big projects. Her instructions are not always clear and she can be difficult, but if you do your work, you will 4.0 easily.

Dr. Ellison is a really great professor, she is extremely kind and cares deeply about her course and the students taking it. The class was very easy, each week we would have a simple homework assignment due at midnight on Fridays, and a simple 5 question quiz on the 1st meeting of the week. The course is simple, you can get an A with little effort

She isn't necessarily a bad professor but her way of lecturing is painfully boring. Attendance policy is overly strict when showing up to the class doesn't really offer much in the way of learning. An easy class just not very enjoyable in any way. Not a bad experience, but also not good

analysis.name: Elizabeth Tinsley Johnson
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I took HBIO295 but it wasn't an option. She was such an amazing teacher! Picky grader but you start to get a grasp of what she wants. The class is very interactive and interesting and I highly recommend

Be prepared to go into a writing class that is a LOT of work. The last thing I expected was to be learning writing techniques as a senior. However, I found Dr. TJ to be amazing. She knows what she is doing. I would 100% take her again and would recommend everyone to take her. It is hard to do poorly in this class as long as you do everything.

Dr. TJ was exactly what every senior needs for their final writing class. She made it clear what needed to be done, was accessible outside of class, and made a personal connection with every student. This class is not SUPER easy because it is long writing, but trust their process and you will be rewarded. There is lots of extra credit as well.

The class structure is very lenient - you can choose which assignments you want to complete each week. The material is very interesting and the class itself is pretty engaging. Professor TJ herself is very well-versed and is a great professor. STEM profs can be too wrapped up in their research, but she's trained in pedagogy which is really nice.

Class is easy, but it's a ton of writing. Lots of discussion boards which is majority of your grade. There is only a final exam, so if you would rather write a lot than take exams I would recommend this class. You can pick and choose what you want to do each week, so class should be an easy 4.0 or 3.5 at least. Book is required for the course.

analysis.name: Jennifer Ekstrom
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 84 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I will never be taking one of her classes again. This class has made me hate nutrition more than I ever thought was possible. She doesn't do any of her actual work, the TAs do everything. Exams are actually INSANE. Never received full credit on my discussion posts because she had to press ONE BUTTON. Save yourself the time and effort. Awful class.

This class was fine, pretty standard for an online class. The tests are a bit hard to prepare for because there are so many terms and things to remember. DONT BUY THE TEXTBOOK! I never bought it and it has had no impact on me. The grad TA for the class was extremely rude but that's not her fault so not part of the rating. Overall, just an ok class.

Lots of work to prepare for exams. Easy online work and quizzes every week as well as discussion posts. Exams are majority of points and require a ton of studying. Recommendation: do all possible extra credit assignments and go to the exam review questions. DO NOT TAKE AS AN ELECTIVE!

Don't recommend at all. We haven't even taken our first exam yet and I'm ready to off myself. Her voice is so monotoned and its hard to grasp information. She reads everything off slides so its hard to learn. If it weren't for attendance I wouldn't be here.

I had professor Jennifer Lynn Ekstrom during the spring semester of 2025. Her lectures were insanely long, her attitude wasn't the best, and she was extremely nitpicky with the grading. She judged what students ate. She got mad when I mentioned my disordered eating and that "I didn't use the resources provided" and I couldn't because of the wait.

analysis.name: Emily Tabuteau
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: There is a LOT you can say about her. She does not use D2L, or much technology at all, her lectures consist of her talking for 50 minutes with a few words on the white board. There is a midterm exam, a final paper, and a final exam, that's it. Tough grader, with the rubrics/syllabus formatted where you almost have to ask her questions.

There is a lot to be said about Professor Tabuteau. She doesn't use D2L so a good chunk of your time will be spent trying to ask her questions about the assignments since she doesn't use rubrics either. She also is weirdly passive aggressive sometimes which made the course that much unbearable.

Emily had a lot of impact on me 30 years ago.  A wonderful professor and teacher.  She lives her history.  An inspriration and I am a professor now.  Tom Eppink, Univ. SC  Take her and see your mind change.
Dr Tabuteau ignited history for me. And more important, she taught me to think.  And write.  And question.  A sterling example of what a professor should be.
Had her class years ago.  She was superb--really taught you how to take apart an argument.  One of the two best professors I had at MSU.

analysis.name: Emilie Jackson
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Jackson was a good economics professor and I enjoyed the class. You're allowed to miss 2–3 classes, but otherwise attendance is mandatory, and there are iClicker questions graded for completion. The homework was challenging, but the exams were relatively easy, and you can drop one exam, which helps.

This class was pretty easy and I even skipped a couple of lectures. Attendence isn't necessary but does factor into the final grade slightly. The exams were relatively easy if you studied beforehand. The homework is very easy. I would recommend this professor and class.

Fine teacher, but her lectures are the worst, and she sometimes does not explain things enough and goes really fast. Not the hardest class ever, but the only class that I actually took away from was one that a TA led.

Prof. Jackson made the class super understandable. There is weekly homework, but your bottom 6 grades get dropped. The exams are super easy, and if you do well on the first 3 you can skip the final since you get to drop an exam. Do not skip class, she does iclicker questions and you get a 15% curve on it which can get you extra credit.

A very likable and overall good teacher. As someone who doesn't know any basic econ, she teaches in a way that helps students to easily understand the topic. Tests are easier than expected. Just review the practice exam and also the Achieve(homework) questions, and you're pretty much set as the questions are basically similar.

analysis.name: Elia Hefner
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 55 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Although my grade in this course was a 2.0 with a 45% on Exam 1, 42.5% on 2, 70% on the 3rd, and an 85% on the 4th, Dr. E is a very caring professor and I can personally attest to that. Very hard class. Be ready to spend a lot of time studying each week. Completely manageable if you know how to balance your other courses with this asynchronous one.

I LOVE professor Hefner, but this class was difficult. I had to retake this course. There is a LOT and I mean a LOT of complicated material per exam & the exams are application based, which the lecture videos don't fully prepare you for. A good grade is possible as long as you don't stack other difficult classes at the same time. Im balding tbh.

As much as I truly do believe Dr. E cares and wants you to do well, it was a struggle. Graded on only 4 exams, minimal EC. Exams are all application, nothing like anything you have seen before or in lectures. I have never worked this hard in a class, still ended with a 3.5, even with meeting Dr. E, office hours, and studying over 20 hours a week.

This class was very hard like ridiculously difficult at one point I had to get a tutor just to pass the class however the professor emphasizes the importance of scheduling and proper studying in order to pass. Lecture clearly show she is passionate and wants student to exceed but the course is graded in so few things making the course so hard.

Just letting you know right now, you'll get extra credit opportunities, but they range to maximum 5.25 points. She genuinely seems like a kind individual, but the setup the class is all online lectures with office hours. What made this class difficult was the exams. That's all you're graded on besides the extra credit. 4 exams and extra credit.

analysis.name: Emily Conroy-Krutz
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: lectures can be boring sometimes and she sometimes talks very fast so it is hard to keep up. You will not pass if you do not show up. She is a great professor and if you like foreign relations you will love this class. I though the papers were actually kinda fun. The quizees are kinda hard, DO THE READINGS. great professor!

This professor deserves a rating higher than 3.2; her class is tough, but it's a college class, and you can't expect an easy A. If you put in just a little more than the minimum amount of work, you'll be fine. She is a very kind professor who you can tell is passionate about history.

A very hard grader. If some people in class do not prepare she punishes the whole class by not explaining the materials. The amount of reading is unreasonable. PowerPoint’s are useless.  rambles, very philosophical,taking notes is hard. course is not organized. Responds to emails very late. Doesn’t acknowledge student’s progress and participation.

When it comes to lectures, the slides give no information and the lectures are reliant on her talking about what is being discussed. She gives multiple readings, some literally being whole books that are 300 pages. When it comes to writing papers, her criteria is horrible and does not explain anything. Just terrible all around to be honest.

Professor Conroy-Krutz was extremely knowledgeable and passionate about her class. There was a lot of reading but that is to be expected from a History class. People on here complaining about her lectures want everything handed to them on a silver platter. If you do the readings and listen/participate during lecture, you will learn a lot.

analysis.name: Emily  Katz
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Katz cares a lot about her students and what they take away from her classes. Second time having her and I'd recommend with my dying breaths tbh. You'll enjoy the class a lot more if you're engaged and participate in discussions, and her study guides make it very easy to excel on the exams given out. Very helpful with papers.

Very good and entertaining professor; provides multiple ways to succeed and cares deeply about the students and the topics covered.

Multiple writing assignments handwritten in class, but a very lenient drop policy allows you to miss classes a couple of times. Exams are strictly based on study guides provided (not many surprise questions).

Katz was the best professor I have had so far. She is very passionate about philosophy and is very clear. She manages to be very interactive in such a big lecture. The study guide and the exams are close to identical, so make sure that you stay on top of that and ATTEND CLASS. You definitely won't pass if you don't come to lecture and take notes.

She's a good professor; knows exactly what she's talking about. However, if you plan on doing at least 5-10 hours of reading a week, this would be the class for you. The reading blocks were very excessive (4 days before class, having 30 pages to read. And 2 days in between classes, having 60 pages to read).

She was a very kind professor. Her lectures were very clear, and she made philosophy pretty interesting for a stem major. you can tell she is very passionate about Philosophy, and she's very experienced. Exams are completely based on the study guides, so if you don't get an A that's on you. Loved her class, highly recommend for IAH

analysis.name: Emily Elliott
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: For HST 201 our final was a 15 page paper. Prof. Elliott is very nice and caring, she gives great feedback on assignments preparing for the paper. She is very easy to get in contact with and responds to emails pretty quickly. She also made it clear that she is always willing to help and care for her students. Very passionate about her job.

Basically half your grade is one paper, but you spent most of the semester just working on it, so it was ok. Elliott is a great speaker, and the class was very entertaining. She would make us work in groups during class sometimes, which was fine but there were some students that made it suck. Clearly very passionate about Russian history.

Prof. Elliot was a very understanding proffessor. She did go through lectures pretty quickly but she does post them at the end of units, but just paying attention helps. There are no tests or quizzes, just 3/4 major writing assignments. She is really timely in replies and you can tell she really enjoys teaching this class. Recitations are also fun!

So, shes a little rude, and she goes through notes a lot faster than some people are prepared for. But, Her assignments are very easy and clearly detailed. 4 assignments including the final. Compared to MSU's other ISS 210 course this one is MUCH easier. The other having almost weekly tests and quizzes.

Professor Elliot lectures every class and then recitation is set up to talk through her lectures and the assigned readings for the week, I found it to be easy because she posts the power points but I would definitely suggest still going to her lectures. There are pop reading quizzes and very few assignments, so try hard and meet the deadlines.

analysis.name: Frederick Engram
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I wish I could give him a zero. He started screaming at us when we had just returned to campus when we had returned from home because he was reported to the dean after he had tryed to have us take a test 2 days after the shooting. He did not support us students, we tried to express our thoughts and feelings and we were screamed at. Avoid him!!!!!

After the MSU shooting, Dr. Engram displayed a lack of empathy towards the students and did not make any changes to the class syllabus, initially asking the class to take an exam two days after the shooting, also continuing to enforce a strict attendance policy. In class, he also tends to ramble and not provide facts or evidence of the things said

I thought a lot of the content he spoke about in class was about his personal opinions not necessarily content from the book. The tests had all content from the book and readings so I was able to study, I just don't agree with his teaching style. I also felt it was hard to give my opinion because if it didn't align with his, it would be a problem.

This professor is not understanding in the slightest, makes it very difficult to get good grades on things like participation! Take any other ISS class if you don't want to absolutely stress about grades.

This professor is a menace. He embarasses students and doesnt put effort into teaching students or making the classroom welcoming. He also does not care about his students especially those who struggle to obtain information or those who are of special needs. If you disagree with him he makes it a huge issue in class

analysis.name: Adam Enders
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Prof was really nice,  but the course layout was not designed for success. Midterm was 30% of the grade, final 35% (cumulative). TopHat was used for lectures/quizzes. While it was nice because I didn't have to go to class, I had to pay for it and I didn't like that. No study guides for the exams and the final covered 472 pages of material. Not easy

If you like long, lecture-based classes (like myself), this course is great. Enders lectured for at least an hour a day and was accompanied by power point slides, which were later posted online. Don't be mistaken, however- this is a very difficult course. But if you want to learn about the ins and outs of congress, it's worth your time and energy.

Instead of using iClickers like other teachers, Professor Enders had us buy a tophat subscription which was pretty annoying. Attendance was supposed to be counted, but due to errors with the app, it wasn't. There are online quizzes every other period, but with the app, you can take them online without showing up if you sign in at the same time.

analysis.name: Eric Juenke
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 40 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Juenke did an amazing job maintaining political neutrality - for every Democratic example, he gave a Republican one, and vice versa. His lectures had humor and great examples. Occasionally, the quiz questions were about small details hidden in the lecture, but as long as you pay attention to the hour-ish lecture, you should be fine.

Best Professor I have had so far. The lectures were engaging and he is incredibly nice. I wish I could take this class again or at least have him for another class. Sadly he only teaches this one, so if you end up with him as a Professor be aware that you probably will never see him again when the class is over.

Amazing Professor, he took the time to explain anything, made assignments clear, made an effort to connect with students, and incorporated real-world events as well as some humor. Had weekly readings and at-home quizzes on the readings and very few other assignments. A very kind and understanding professor I cant recommend him enough.

This was a really good class !! He takes IClicker attendance every class but you get 4 drops. there's weekly quizzes but if you pay attention to the lecture slides you'll be fine. There's also a lot of quizlets for the class. Overall great professor, very understanding, I would take his class again !!

Dr. Juenke is my favorite. His lecture slides are sometimes confusing and feel disorganized, but I also am the type of person who color codes everything so that could just be me. Juenke genuinely cares about his students. He remembers names and is extremely approachable. I didn't get a 4.0, but I enjoyed his class a lot: it felt meaningful.

analysis.name: Richard Enbody
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 70 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: This dude is hands down the most booty professor at MSU, literally the class is the equivalent to a doctor diagnosing you with cancer and then telling you to figure out the treatment by yourself. The help room blows cause theres 2 TA's helping out 150 + students so its impossible to get anything done. And the exams might give you aids.

He is pure evil. I finally understand why he cancelled lecture and let students read textbooks and watch videos instead. So he can earn extra money from textbooks he wrote but also saving time on prepare lecture and teach lecture! How convenient! In this way, we are "forced" to buy textbooks or we will literally not learn anything from this class.

A heartless sociopath of a professor, whose exam's are notoriously difficult - I managed to get straight hundreds on the programs yet the tests are formatted in such a way that if you miss one question in one section of the test, you'll miss all of the ones relating to that problem. He refuses to curve  grades and is completely unhelpful.  0/10 IGN
Pretentious refusal to curve incredibly difficult exams. Excessive homework, but manageable.

Definitely not recommended. I am a 4.0 student and got nearly 100% on all projects but almost failed because of how the exams are. To clarify, they are never curved and if you miss one question, it is almost guaranteed to snowball into losing a significant chunk of points.
